articleTitle: Comparison of Josephson Impedance Bridges
abstract: The first two impedance bridges based on pulse-driven Josephson voltage standards show the lowest uncertainties among digital bridges even comparable with state-of-the-art bridges using inductive voltage divider. In this paper, we will present the world’s first comparison between these bridges. The observed difference between both systems measuring impedance ratios (C:C and R:R) is 6 nF/F and 6 nΩ/Ω at 1233.15 Hz. Up to 50 kHz, the measurements from both bridges agree within uncertainties, which are still below one part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> and dominated by cable effects.

articleTitle: Long-term Study on Travelling Standards for Capacitance and Resistance
abstract: We have investigated the long-term properties of two 10 nF capacitance standards and two resistance standards of 10 kΩ and 12.9 kΩ over a period of almost four years. All four standards are integrated into the same two-stage thermostat. The observed daily drift is approximately -1 nF/F for both capacitance standards and less than -2 nΩ/Ω for the resistance standards. The temperature controller is equipped with back-up batteries to supply the thermostat during power failures (black out) and transport. Due to this feature, the standards took part in the first comparison between pulse-driven Josephson impedance bridges.

articleTitle: Trilateral Comparison Among Digital and Josephson Impedance Bridges
abstract: In this work, we present the results of an onsite trilateral comparison between a dual Josephson impedance bridge developed by METAS and the electronic fully-digital impedance bridges developed by CMI and INRIM-POLITO. The target accuracies of the bridges are at the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup> level for the former and at the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−7</sup> for the latter. Here we report the results of the calibration of a 10nF capacitance standard against a 12.9kΩ calculable resistance standard at 1233Hz, conditions suitable for the primary direct realization of the impedance units ohm and farad from AC quantum Hall resistance standards or from AC/DC calculable transfer resistance standards calibrated against DC quantum Hall resistance standards.

articleTitle: Calibration of Magnitude Error of Lock-in Amplifiers and Noise Response
abstract: In this work the calibration of the magnitude error and the noise response of a digital lock-in amplifier are presented. A simple but effective calibration setup developed at INRIM is used to assess the magnitude error of a recent model of lock-in amplifier. The noise response of the instrument is analyzed in terms of Allan deviation for different filter orders.

articleTitle: Research on Mass Measurement Difference Between Joule Balance and Primary Mass Standard
abstract: It is important to perform a stability check for the joule balance after the redefinition of kilogram. A research on the mass measurement difference between the joule balance and primary mass standard is proposed in this paper. The measurement results form three different ways have been compared and analyzed. The experiments showed that the mass measurement results based on the joule balance and primary mass standards can meet with each other within the relative standard uncertainty of 4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>.

articleTitle: Tunable Sensitivity Enhancement of a Rydberg-Atom Electrometer
abstract: This paper presents a metallic resonant cavity for sensitivity enhancement of a Rydberg atom microwave electrometer. The Rubidium-filled vapor cell is encased by the resonator, with appropriate coupling structures for laser beams and the incident radio-frequency field. The resonator is designed to enhance the sensitivity of Rydberg states from 10.19 to 10.77GHz with 620MHz of frequency tunability. The resonator exhibits an intrinsic Q-factor ranging from 4546 to 5520, for ultimate field enhancement factors ranging from 3.5 to 9.3.

articleTitle: Traceable Measurements of Mutual Inductance Standards Applied to Large Capacitance Simulation in Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy
abstract: This summary paper presents the results for establishing traceable mutual inductance measurements at low frequencies. The measurements performed were validated by comparing the results with an established fully-digital impedance bridge. The use of mutual inductors for the simulation of high capacitance values and its potential use for calibration of electrochemical impedance spectroscopy meters is discussed.

articleTitle: A New Resistive Voltage Divider with Self-Calibration
abstract: A novel resistive voltage divider with fewer signal relays has been developed to realize rapid and accurate self-calibration. Analysis of the principle demonstrates the feasibility of the self-calibration of this resistive voltage divider. Preliminary experiments in direct current have been conducted to reveal a relative standard deviation of less than 5.0 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>.

articleTitle: Leakage Current Pathways in Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer Standards
abstract: The voltage errors associated with leakage currents in Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizer (JAWS) systems are significant contributors to the overall system accuracy. This paper describes discrepancies in output voltage between two different circuit halves on a single JAWS chip and shows that this discrepancy is dominated by ac leakage currents through the stray capacitance in the compensation leads.

articleTitle: The Upgraded CERN DC-current Calibrator
abstract: An improved version of the CERN DC-current Calibrator (CDC) is presented. The CDC is a programmable, high precision, high resolution, +/- 10 A DC current source, initially developed for the calibration and testing of Direct-Current Current Transformers (DCCTs) used in the powering of superconducting magnets in the Large Hadron Collider at CERN. The upgrade addresses the stricter stability and low-frequency noise requirements for the testing of DCCTs for the new High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) project.

articleTitle: An Improved 10 mA /10 V Standard for the CERN DC-current Calibrator
abstract: An improved 10 V / 10 mA standard is presented, which is part of the test infrastructure for direct current current transformers (DCCTs) for the High Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) project at CERN. It serves primarily as a reference source for the 10 A CERN DC-current calibrator, but also as a 10 V source with extremely low noise at sub-Hz frequencies. Improvements were made in the internal voltage reference and voltage-to-current conversion circuits. Measurements against the PTB programmable Josephson voltage standard (PJVS) show 1/f noise-limited Allan deviation at 10 V on the order of 5•10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup> V for measurement times of seconds to hours.

articleTitle: Progress of the BIPM Pilot Studies on Differential Measurements of an ac Source with Programmable Josephson Voltage Standards
abstract: BIPM performed two pilot studies in 2023 to support the uncertainty budget for the programmable Josephson voltage standard (PJVS). The studies involved differential sampling with an ac source, as proposed in the new BIPM on-site comparison protocol. Sinewave signals of 1 V rms at different frequencies (62.5 Hz, 125 Hz, 250 Hz, 625 Hz, 1250 Hz) were investigated with PTB and KRISS. The results exhibited excellent repeatability and reproducibility when comparing measurements with two identical PJVS systems based on the KRISS voltage standard. Conversely, the comparison of two different PJVS systems (BIPM and PTB PJVS systems) led to divergent results. The suspected cause of the discrepancy is likely the presence of larger leakage-current-induced errors on the BIPM PJVS setup. Further pilot studies will be performed in 2024 to resolve this problem.

articleTitle: Differential Measurements of an AC Source with a Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer
abstract: This paper describes differential sampling measurements of an ac source and a Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizer (JAWS). A new iterative approach for aligning the phases of the JAWS and the source waveforms was implemented to minimize the differential voltage at the digitizer. A type-A uncertainty of 45 nV/V after 10 min was measured for a commercial ac source at 1 V rms amplitude and 1 kHz.

articleTitle: Status report on the BIPM Kibble Balance
abstract: This paper reports the latest advances on the Kibble balance that the BIPM maintains for realizing the definition of the mass unit. The BIPM successfully participated in the first and second key comparisons of realizations of the kilogram, and carried out new measurements for the third one. Various refinements were made to the apparatus including the validation of the operation of a new PJVS array cooled inside a cryocooler. Characterization of the first prototype of a double-pan new beam mechanism was completed. An improved mechanism based on a single-pan beam balance has been designed and fabricated.

articleTitle: Stability Study of ac Voltage Source using Josephson Voltage Standards
abstract: The stability of an ac voltage source fabricated at the National Research Council Canada (NRC) is investigated. In this work, differential sampling was used to monitor the source voltage with respect to a step-wise approximated reference waveform generated by the Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard (PJVS) at 4 V and at 1 V. The frequency dependence of the source error is extracted, and the same measurements are repeated 13.5 months later to determine the long-term stability. Different digitizers are used to evaluate input filter effects. The NRC ac voltage source is found to be a suitable travelling standard with a stability of < 4 µV/V per year. At the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), differential sampling was used to monitor the difference between a Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer (JAWS) at 1 V and this source. Information is obtained about the effect of relative humidity on the source phase.

articleTitle: Toward Precision Resistance Measurements by a Precision LCR Meter at Frequencies up to 2 MHz
abstract: We have investigated the lead effects of a 10-kΩ resistance standard measured by a precision LCR meter at frequencies up to 2 MHz. In the case of a two-terminal-pair configuration, we demonstrate that the effect of 2.5 m long measuring leads, which are inevitable for some special applications, can be precisely corrected. Other systematic effects of the LCR meter were also investigated. They are distinctly larger than the resolution of the LCR meter, but accurately reproducible. As such it should be possible to calibrate the LCR meter against a calculable high-frequency resistance standard with an uncertainty close to the few-parts-per-million resolution of the LCR meter.

articleTitle: Development of a beam mechanism for the BIPM Kibble Balance
abstract: This paper reports the advances on the development of a new beam mechanism for the BIPM Kibble balance. The first prototype double-pan balance beam mechanism was characterized on a test set-up in air. Key features of the first prototype design were successfully checked. A revised beam based on a single-pan design has been fabricated and recently integrated in the setup. Control of the set-up and characterization of the mechanism behavior will start soon.

articleTitle: Measurement Repeatability of a Supercapacitor Equivalent Circuit Parameters
abstract: The determination of the equivalent parameters of a supercapacitor requires the galvanostatic measurement of a charge and self-discharge cycle. If a more general determination is needed than that on the single cycle, it is necessary to take into account the repeatability of the charging and self-discharging cycles. A cycle can also extend over a few hours for larger supercapacitors. Therefore, having a large set of cycles including the time required for parameters determination is definitely a time-consuming procedure. In this work, an efficient method for the repeatability assessment of the equivalent circuit parameters is proposed; this approach relies on a limited set of experimental curves and on a single parameter identification process.

articleTitle: Longitudinal Impedance Measurements on Graphene QHE Devices
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges associated with accurately measuring longitudinal impedance in a quantum Hall device. A novel bridge design capable of measuring both real and imaginary components of longitudinal impedance is introduced and applied for the first time. The measured inductance appears to be independent of both carrier density and mobility. Additionally, the inductance remains constant over the frequency range from 600 Hz to 50 kHz.

articleTitle: Bilateral comparison of planar multijunction thermal converters maintained at CMI and SUT
abstract: The paper describes a bilateral comparison of a set of planar multijunction thermal converters (PMJTC) maintained at the Czech Metrology Institute (CMI) and the Silesian University of Technology (SUT), Poland, at 1 V and selected frequencies from 10 Hz to 1 MHz. The comparison shows good agreement among the AC-DC transfer differences of SUT and CMI standards. The analysis shows that above approximately 700 kHz, the SUT and CMI standards differ in their AC-DC voltage transfer differences, but these differences, below 5 µV/V, are still within measurement uncertainties.

articleTitle: Impact of Sampler Characteristics in a PJVS-Based Differential Sampling: A Comparative Analysis of Measurements Using Fluke 8588A and NI PXI-5922
abstract: We conducted an in-depth investigation into the impact of measurement circuit configuration, sampler gain error, sampling-trigger delay settings, and the built-in filter function of the sampler on the accuracy of quantum-based differential sampling of AC waveforms. Our main focus was on Fluke 8588A and NI PXI-5922 samplers with wide bandwidths exceeding 3 MHz and identifying the conditions under which these two samplers gave equivalent measurement results at the 1 kHz frequency level.

articleTitle: On alternative traceability chains of impedance units with digital impedance bridges
abstract: We discuss the calibration schemes for disseminating the capacitance unit farad from the reference resistance standard. The impedance ratio measurements are performed with a fully digital bridge. High stability and low crosstalk of the involved generators SWG able to perform extreme impedance ratio scaling up to 129:1. We introduce the idea of involving calculable resistance standards, which enable the laboratory to perform realization of the whole capacitance scale from DC QHE with only one DC resistance bridge and one digital bridge. Further, an alternative involvement of a single AC Josephson source is proposed. A practical example is given to demonstrate the discussed traceability chains.

articleTitle: Thin-Film Resistance Standards with Calculable AC-DC Difference at Frequencies up to 2 MHz
abstract: We have developed novel 12.906 kΩ impedance standards based on series-connected thin-film resistors. The frequency dependence is calculable at frequencies up to a few megahertz and, due to the small thin-films dimensions, several orders of magnitude smaller than for all conventional calculable resistors at a comparable nominal value and smaller than the resolution of commercial precision LCR meters. The calculation and the experimental verification will be presented at the conference. In future, this will allow the calibration of precision LCR meters with an unmatched relative uncertainty of a few parts per million in the frequency range up to 2 MHz.

articleTitle: Inter-Laboratory Comparison of Transfer Standard for DC Power Measurements in Nominal and Distorted Conditions
abstract: The metrological characterization of DC static meters in normal operating conditions poses several challenges, both from a methodological and technological point of view. This paper presents the preliminary results of an inter-laboratory comparison between METAS and INRIM. The obtained results have two objectives: to prove the stability of the reference systems, and to assess the possible effects of AC disturbances in DC power measurements.

articleTitle: Metrology support for enhanced energy efficiency in DC transportation systems
abstract: This paper describes a new EU-co-funded project on metrology support for enhanced energy efficiency in DC transportation systems (e-TRENY). The project involves 5 national metrology institutes, 3 universities, 1 metro operator, and 1 consulting group. Research focuses on the following topics: i) new calibration facilities for DC transducers (up to 3 kV, 1 kA) under dynamic conditions, ii) accurate on-site losses of the converter group (power transformer – AC/DC bidirectional converter, DC/DC converter) operating in DC substations, iii) energy saving performance of transportation systems with non-conventional DC substations.

articleTitle: A Stable, Programmable Current Source for the NIM-2 Joule Balance
abstract: The current source is used to produce a stable electromagnetic force in the joule balance method to realize the kilogram. The stability of the current determines the statistical uncertainty of the force measurement. In this paper, an approach of two-stage current parallel-summation is proposed to realize the coarse and fine tuning separately, which is controlled by two digital-to-analog converters to set-up different voltage references. In addition, the distributed array of resistors and a 1‰ voltage divider are built for higher precision of the output. A programmable current source with the stability better than 0.1 ppm/5min (5 mA) and high-resolution (0.07 nA) is developed.

articleTitle: Digital Multimeters Sampling Performance Comparison
abstract: This paper reports on an evaluation of the Keysight 3458A (DMM1) and Fluke 8588A (DMM2) digital multimeter sampling performance and their comparison for white noise, 1/f noise, time jitter related noise and AC linearity. The design of two DMMs shows limitations in performance as a sampler, indicating their application applicability and areas for further research.

articleTitle: Determination of the capacitance gradient of the LNE electrostatic balance: weighings and direct measurements
abstract: The LNE is developing a measuring device using an electrostatic force generator for the realization of small masses and forces in the International System of Units (SI). The weighing mechanism is completely monolithic and can support two capacitive actuators. In this paper, we have focused on two methods for measuring the capacitance gradient dC/dz: by applying the known weight of a standard mass or by measuring the capacitance at different vertical position.

articleTitle: Study on the Calibration of Partial Discharge Calibrators of charge from 0.1pC to 10nC
abstract: This paper describes NIM’s measurement methods for Partial Discharge(PD) calibrators of 10nC and below 1pC in 2023 for participation of supplementary comparison EURAMET.EM-s36. Because the comparison range is from 0.1pC to 10nC, which is very wide. The impulse voltage signals are from a few millivolts to tens of volts, therefore different measurement methods are applied by NIM for low signal levels and strong signal levels in order to obtain low measurement uncertainty. It is difficult for the numerical integration method recommended in IEC60270-2015. Therefore, in this work the measuring resistor is not a single low-inductance resistor. But a set of low-inductance resistors ranging from 5Ω to 2kΩ are developed. For charge below 1pC, a voltage preamplifier is applied to amplify and improve the signals.

articleTitle: Temperature Controller for the Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer
abstract: This paper presents a cryocooled Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizer (JAWS) developed at the National Institute of Metrology (NIM), China. A 2-volt Josephson junction chip is mounted on the second stage cold head of a cryostat. We develop a temperature controller to measure the output voltage of the temperature sensor, and control the temperature of the second-stage cold head. The controller is composed of a current source of high stability, relays, a preamplifier, a low pass filter and a 24-bit analog to digital converter, and a microcontroller unit. Preliminary results show that the cooling power at 4.2 K is about 279 mW and the temperature fluctuation is within 40 mK.

articleTitle: Design of an Analyser for DC Power Quality Measurements in between Electric Vehicles and Rapid Chargers
abstract: The increase in the use of electric vehicles (EV) has caused a growth in EV chargers, which incorporate DC metering to bill consumers. These EV chargers can generate electrical disturbances superimposed on the DC that interfere with the metering if it has insufficient immunity to this DC power quality (PQ) phenomena. This paper describes the design of an analyser to measure DC PQ . The specifications and constraints of the DC PQ analyser are given, with a detailed plan of the instrument components and assembly. The paper also explains the measurement requirements for the validation of the analyser. It is necessary to measure the DC PQ in between EVs and their DC chargers to ensure that the DC metering standards such as IEC 62052-11 applied, are appropriate for the distortions present.

articleTitle: Parallelization of charge-pumps in silicon for practical realization of the SI ampere
abstract: The direct realization of the ampere in the International System of Units is based on precise control of electron transport across a quantum dot to generate an accurate benchmark current. Practical implementation of this technology for dc-current metrology demands an output current of at least hundreds of microamperes within a relative uncertainty below sub-parts-per-million. Here, we propose a physical architecture of a cryogenic dc-source-module that incorporates several charge-pumps in parallel on a single-chip to potentially fulfill the metrological requirement. The total current produced by the dc-source-module is given by the summation of the quantized current collected from individual charge-pumps while transferring single-electrons per voltage cycle.

articleTitle: Development of stable high-resistance standard resistors
abstract: Japan Finechem Company and NMIJ/AIST have developed stable high-resistance standard resistors for over a decade. The prototype 10 TΩ and 100 TΩ standard resistors showed stable resistance change during the comparison with domestic companies/institutes in Japan and with VSL. The drift rates per year of the recent few years are +13.0 μΩ/Ω and −14.7 μΩ/Ω, respectively.

articleTitle: Dynamic force generation capabilities in the PB2 Planck-Balance
abstract: This contribution presents the generation of dynamic force in a table top Kibble balance. The inertial force of a mass standard that is moved in an oscillatory motion is determined in a dynamic force mode and serves as known reference force. Particular uncertainty contributions of the dynamic force mode are discussed.

articleTitle: Characterization of Digitally Modulated Signals at Millimeter-wave Frequency Bands up to 100 GHz
abstract: In this paper, a vector network analyzer (VNA) based precisely synchronized setup is presented for digitally modulated-signal measurements up to 100 GHz. To achieve frequency extension towards 100 GHz, two external passive harmonic mixers are utilized to down-convert the millimeter-wave components of 64-QAM test signal and multisine phase reference to the microwave band, which are later measured by the VNA receivers with a limited frequency band less than 67 GHz. Power and phase calibrations are performed to correct the systematic errors of frequency-domain measurements, so that time-domain waveform can be reconstructed for digital demodulation. By applying pre-distortion according to calibrated measurements, the error vector magnitude (EVM) of user-defined 64-QAM signals can be lowered. According to the experimental results at 94.5 and 100.5 GHz under a 64-QAM symbol rate of 100 MSymbol/s, the nominal EVM values of pre-distorted signals is from 0.91% to 2.45% in this work.

articleTitle: Finite-Element Simulations of the Effects of Shielding and Guarding of a Capacitor Using Coaxial Cylindrical Electrodes for Electrostatic Force Balance Measurements
abstract: This work reports investigations of the possible effects of shielding and guarding of a capacitor using coaxial cylindrical electrodes on the capacitance gradient determination in electrostatic force balance measurements. The capacitances of capacitors using coaxial cylindrical electrodes were calculated by the finite-element method (FEM) in a condition that the shielding/guarding electrode of the capacitor is open or semi-closed using a metal lid on the shielding electrode. The results showed that the residuals from the linear fit in the capacitance gradient determination in the open-shielding case attained almost identical values to those in the semi-closed-shielding case, which was confirmed by experiments using a voltage balance apparatus. The FEM results also suggested that the grounding of the capacitor can have a considerable impact on the mass and force determination using the electrostatic force based on the capacitance measurements.

articleTitle: Measurement methodology in photon momentum based laser power/small force measurements
abstract: In this contribution the methodology adopted for photon momentum based small force (and the average power of lasers) measurements will be discussed. A brief outline of a) the possible ways to calibrate the measurement scales of various instruments, b) the short-, direct-, and unbroken SI traceability chain of the measurement quantities to primary standards, based on the governing equation underlying the photon momentum method, and c) in particular example of the table-top Photon Momentum setup employing the Kibble balance (Planck-Balance) principle, one of the building blocks of methodology i.e. the interferometric length measurements with newly developed Range-Resolved-Interferometer concept will be detailed.

articleTitle: A harmonic analysis method based on quadratic weighting
abstract: This paper introduces a quadratic weighted Fourier transform method based on quasi-synchronous sampling, which can solve the problems of transition process, Gibbs effect and asynchronous sampling when programmable Josephson quantum voltage standard is applied to harmonic voltage measurement by two different weighted and two step correction of the original signal obtained from differential sampling. According to the preliminary verification, when FLUKE 5700A is used as the voltage source, the standard deviation of the signal measurement results in the range of 1 kHz is consistent in the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>.

articleTitle: Evaluation of S-Parameter/Impedance Measurement System Frequency up to 110 GHz with waveguide connector at CMS
abstract: In this year, we are evaluating our Scattering-parameter/ Impedance measurement system and extending the measurement frequencies range up to 110 GHz at CMS (Center for Measurement Standards) in Taiwan. The evaluated method of vector network analyzer (VNA) is based on metrology guide EURAMET cg-12 [1]. It is shown in this paper that the WR10 waveguide connector type evaluation result of the measurement uncertainties of VAN. We have designed CCD vision position platform to ensure that the coaxial and waveguide type connector could be paralleled.

articleTitle: The national capacitance standard on basis of the new vertical calculable cross-capacitor at NIM
abstract: The national capacitance standard on basis of the new vertical calculable cross-capacitor (VCCC) of 0.4 pF with the standard uncertainty of 0.01 μF/F at NIM is authorized since March 2023 in China. In the meantime, a new type vacuum toroidal cross-capacitor (TCC) with a nominal value of 1 pF has been developed as a substitute to maintain the capacitance unit and a transfer standard capacitor to perform intercomparisons in future. The mean cross capacitance determined by comparison to the new VCCC, is confirmed to be better than 0.03 μF/F per year.

Author Keywords: latest optimal hollow active auxiliary electrode

articleTitle: High-accuracy measurements of the quantum anomalous Hall effect for resistance metrology
abstract: This study explores the quantum anomalous Hall effect (QAHE) in V-doped (BiSb)2Te3, a magnetically-doped topological insulators. We use a precision resistance bridge based on a cryogenic current comparator to measure the QAHE at a zero magnetic field with unprecedented uncertainty (ΔRxy/RK ≤ 12 nΩ/Ω). Measurement results obtained at currents between 40 and 300 nA demonstrate the potential of this technology for quantum metrology, offering a path to a primary electrical resistance standard without external magnetic fields.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis of Mechanical Imperfections in the LNE Thompson-Lampard Calculable Capacitor Standard
abstract: This paper describes briefly an electrostatic finite element simulation study of the imperfections of the LNE Thompson-Lampard calculable capacitor (TLCC) and their contributions to the standard’s uncertainty. Thus, the limits of the accepted tolerances in order to achieve the target relative uncertainty of one part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> of the capacitance standard can be established. The simulation predictions are compared with experimental observations with the help of the sub-micron level control of the capacitor standard’s electrode geometry.

articleTitle: Evaluating Aging Uncertainty of Impedance Standard Substrate in On-wafer S-parameter Measurements
abstract: The behavior and performance of RF on-wafer planar calibration circuits change throughout their lifetime. To understand the limits of operation and how the environment affects the performance of reference wafers, accelerated thermal aging tests are conducted to simulate real-world harsh conditions. The aging errors of on-wafer devices measured before and after thermal aging are found to be smaller than the contact repeatability of RF probing up to 50 GHz.

articleTitle: Applications and Limitations of the Kibble-Robinson Theory
abstract: Ten years ago, B. Kibble and I. Robinson published an article that promised a simplification of the Kibble balance experiment. According to this theory, the effect of parasitic forces and non-vertical motions cancel if the position and orientation of the coil are given by a single degree of freedom. We reiterate the derivation of the Kibble-Robinson theory (KRT) and then paraphrase the theory to emphasize the assumptions and conclusions. From there, we discuss the implications of the difference measurement in force mode, the effect of corner loading, the addition of relief gimbals, and the non-verticality of the sensing direction.

articleTitle: Summary of CCEM Key Comparison CCEM.RF-K26: Attenuation at 18 GHz, 26.5 GHz and 40 GHz using a Step Attenuator
abstract: This paper summarizes the results of the Key Comparison CCEM.RF-K26: Attenuation at 18 GHz, 26.5 GHz and 40 GHz using a step attenuator which has been performed from January 2015 to February 2018. Fourteen National Metrology Institutes (NMIs) participated in this key comparison, and the Key Comparison Reference Values (KCRVs) were determined from the measurement results of five to ten participating NMIs, depending on the attenuation and frequency.

articleTitle: A Suitable Method to Obtain and Compare AC-DC Difference Loading Errors of Thermal Transfer Standards
abstract: This paper describes a suitable method to obtain and compare the loading effects of thermal transfer standards to obtain optimal values of input impedance and the AC-DC difference loading errors. The loading effects are evaluated with different values of source series-connected resistance and a bypass capacitance at desired frequencies and applied voltages. The results indicate that the AC-DC difference loading errors are minimized with a nominal source series-connected resistance value of 50 Ω, and a bypass capacitance value in the range of 33 pF to 68 pF.

articleTitle: Measurement of Phase Angle Error of Reference Micropotentiometer Resistors
abstract: This paper presents preliminary results of phase angle error measurements of several radial thin-film micro-potentiometer resistors developed at the National Measurement Institute, Australia (NMIA). We explore the viability of using these resistors as references for phase error measurements of current shunts and precision resistors. The effects of common mode dependence and level dependence have been investigated. The measurements were made for a range of frequencies from 40 Hz to 100 kHz. Preliminary results demonstrate that the phase angle error of two resistors that are compared directly, and the sum of phase angle errors of two comparisons to a third resistor show agreement of better than 5 µrad.

articleTitle: Dielectric Waveguide as Transmission Line for R 1.8k Microcalorimeter
abstract: A dielectric waveguide can exhibit lower insertion loss than a metal waveguide at millimeter wave and sub-millimeter wave frequencies, and thus is an excellent candidate for a transmission line in the development of a new microcalorimeter set-up for frequencies up to 220 GHz. The realized transmission line presented in this paper consists of the dielectric waveguide itself as well as the transitions to the rectangular metal waveguide interface type R 1.8k (WR 5). Simulation and measurement data are shown.

articleTitle: Development of Graphene Quantum Hall Effect AC Metrology at RISE
abstract: We present the first steps taken towards a graphene quantum Hall effect ac resistance standard at RISE. A new measurement setup has been developed including a graphene quantum Hall effect device suitable for the kilohertz range and a coaxial cryoprobe to be used together with a coaxial impedance bridge based on inductive voltage dividers. 1:1 ratio resistance measurements of the graphene device against a 12.9 kΩ ac resistance standard resulted in a linear frequency dependent (≈ 0.2 (µΩ/Ω)/kHz) deviation from the quantized dc value.

articleTitle: Improvement of the dynamic phase measurement noise of the LNE Kibble balance by the implementation of a linear motor
abstract: The determination of a mass value in a Kibble balance type experiment requires the determination of the geometric factor of the magnetic circuit - coil set by two different methods. One of these phases requires the simultaneous acquisition of voltage and speed, the associated measurement noise must be reduced to the lowest possible value. This paper presents the improvement in the signal-to-noise ratio of the geometric factor by replacing the existing screw motor with a linear motor. The noise of the geometrical factor is reduced by a factor of five, which ultimately decreases the noise associated with the determination of the value of a mass in the LNE Kibble balance by a factor of five.

articleTitle: Recent update on the Tsinghua tabletop Kibble balance
abstract: The primary objective of the Tsinghua tabletop Kibble balance experiment is to develop a compact, high-precision, user-friendly, and cost-effective apparatus for mass realization, particularly within the kilogram range. In this concise overview, we outline the advancements made in the Tsinghua tabletop Kibble balance project. We provide insights into the progress of key components, including electrical, magnetic, mechanical, and optical elements. Additionally, noteworthy measurement results, such as the determination of absolute gravitational acceleration and the characterization of the magnet system, are presented for a comprehensive understanding of the experiment’s status.

articleTitle: An Alternative Calorimetric Approach for Power Loss Measurement of Ultra-efficient Power Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a calorimeter design for efficiency measurement of ultra-efficient power electronics. The proposed configuration utilizes a closed single-chamber, double-jacketed construction with a temperature-controlled heater. The main objective of the new design is to reduce measurement complexity without compromising accuracy. This is accomplished by measuring the change in electrical input power of the heating element while the controller maintains constant temperature, which serves as a measure of the losses of the power electronics.

articleTitle: Redetermination of the Gravitational Constant using the BIPM Torsion Balance
abstract: For the past several years, we have been using the torsion balance developed at the Bureau International des Poids et Mesures (BIPM) to measure the gravitational constant G. The most notable feature of the apparatus is that it allows the measurement of G with two different methods: the Cavendish method and the Servo method.The systematic effects are different in several important variables, leading to an improved combined result. In the past year, we have identified a gas pressure effect that hampered previous measurements at the National Institute of Standards and Technology

articleTitle: Accurate resistance comparators with ratiometric digital multimeters
abstract: This summary paper describes and characterizes two resistance comparators exploiting long-scale digital multimeters operating in ratiometric mode and compares the results obtained in the measurement of resistance ratios of 12.906kΩ : 10kΩ and 10kΩ : 1kΩ against those obtained with a direct current comparator. The comparators herewith described are suitable for primary resistance metrology with accuracy at the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup>–10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−7</sup> level, depending on the resistance ratio.

articleTitle: Measurement of the Magnetic Dipole Moment At Variable Temperature
abstract: A measurement device for magnetic dipole moment of permanent magnets at different temperatures is built. In order to achieve in-situ measurement at variable temperature in open magnetic circuit state, the rotating sample method is used. This paper focuses on the design of non-magnetic high temperature and low temperature furnaces respectively, and the temperature calibration. The results of ten times repeat measurement on NdFeB magnet show that the relative standard deviation is not more than 0.12%, the expanded uncertainty of magnetic dipole moment is 0.49%-0.70% (k=2).

articleTitle: Errors in a cryogenic current comparator at low flux levels
abstract: We present preliminary ratio accuracy tests on a 10000:10000 ratio cryogenic current comparator (CCC) at microamp current levels. We observe an error flux in the CCC’s SQUID detector of ∼ 4 μϕ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> which does not reverse sign when the bridge current source high and low terminals are exchanged. We discuss the possible implications for precision scaling of small currents and electron pump measurements.

articleTitle: Truncated M-sequence and BOC Modulation based Ranging Signal Design for TWSTFT
abstract: TWSTFT is a representative time comparison technique mostly using a bent-pipe transponder of a GEO satellite with Ku-band frequency. Conventionally, DS-BPSK-based signal structures have been used for global TWSTFT links among NMIs. The BPSK-based signal structure has the advantage of having a simple transceiver structure but is inappropriate for long coherent integration time in correlation processing. Also, BPSK-based ACF have relatively wide main lobe width and low sharpness waveform. Those ACF properties cause signal-tracking performance degradation. Conventional TWSTFT code sequence sets have relatively high cross-correlation power levels. Properties of those code sequence sets are inappropriate for service to multi-user simultaneously. In this paper, a BOC and Truncated M-sequence based new TWSTFT signal structure was proposed for improving those conventional signals. To evaluate the new TWSTFT signal structure and its code sequence sets, PSD, processing gain, ACFs, and cross-correlation power levels were compared with those of conventional SATRE, SRS modem, and GPS L1C/A, L1Cp signals.

Author Keywords: Two-Way Satellite Time and Frequency Transfer

articleTitle: Methods of Zero Thermal Offset Compensation and Precision Measurements Using a Microvolt-level Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: In order to enhance the accuracy of low-voltage measurement based on the double Josephson junction arrays on one chip developed at NIM, a method has been proposed for compensating thermal voltages on precision measurement leads, with the practical details. Better results have been obtained. The reading error of typical point e.g. at ±1 µV with a few nV smaller than before. When the system was built to be performed as an instrument like a digital voltmeter (DVM) to calibrate a dc reference, an optimized operation is presented to improve performance particularly for low-voltage measurement.

articleTitle: SI Traceable RF and Microwave Power Measurements at Cryogenic Temperatures
abstract: This work demonstrates SI traceable RF and microwave power measurements at cryogenic temperatures down to 3 K using a commercial balance thermoelectric type power sensor. This is the first time, to the best of our knowledge, a commercial RF power sensor has been tested at such cryogenic temperatures. To obtain SI traceability, a power sensor’s thermopile response was characterized over RF power levels from -35 dBm to 0 dBm in a frequency range from 100 kHz to 10 GHz using known DC power. The thermopile response was then utilized to calculate absolute RF power around 3 K. The results demonstrated suitability of the power sensor to operate at temperatures down to 3 K and RF and microwave power levels down to -35 dBm.

articleTitle: 300 mV Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer Chip in NIM
abstract: This paper describes the current status of developing Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizer (JAWS) chips in NIM (National Institute of Metrology, China). The chip has one data input channel and two Josephson junction arrays, each array consisted by 4000 double-stack Nb/Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1–x</inf>/Nb junctions. The two arrays were driven with a single pulse-generator channel by using one on-chip Wilkinson power divider and inside/outside DC blocks. Root-mean-square (rms) output magnitude of 300 mV was generated with this JAWS chip.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Multitone Signal Characterization Using the AC Quantum Voltmeter
abstract: This article presents a new method for characterizing multi-tone signals measured with an AC quantum voltmeter. Using a four period signal from the programmable Josephson voltage standard, we overcome the previously missing short portions of the signal measured due to the transients. As an example, we show measurements and analyses of a two-tone signal with different fundamental frequencies and amplitudes. For these waveforms, we calculate the root mean square voltage and the harmonic content of the tones. The results obtained agree better than 1 μV/V with the expected values.

articleTitle: Calibration of room-temperature ratio bridge with graphene quantum Hall array device
abstract: We describe the preliminary measurement conducted to establish a baseline dataset toward a cryogen-free system for quantized Hall resistance (QHR) standard application. This paper illustrates the current state-of-the-art cryogenic system, the quantization verification and ratio measurement between an established GaAs Hall bar and a graphene-base quantum Hall array resistance standard (GQHARS). The technology comparison is carried out with a room temperature ratio bridge.

articleTitle: Satellite radio detection via dual-microwave Rydberg spectroscopy
abstract: Rydberg electric field sensors exploit the structured multitude of electronic transitions between Rydberg atomic states. In this way, they can detect electric fields with frequencies spanning DC to THz. However, difficulty accessing resonant transitions at ultra-high frequencies (UHF, 0.3-30 GHz) and below hinders their applicability within this ubiquitous band of the world’s wireless communications infrastructure. We present a Rydberg electric field sensor operating in the UHF band using a resonant dual-optical dual-microwave spectroscopy scheme. This enables access to transitions with lower resonant frequencies, and higher angular momentum (L = 3→4), than those typically used in Rydberg sensors. We measure the resonant sensitivity of our system at 2.3 GHz to be 70(5) µVm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1/2</sup>, 50 times better than the measured sensitivity with a far off-resonant probing scheme at this frequency. Moreover, we demonstrate the effectiveness of this scheme by measuring Sirius XM satellite radio (2.320 - 2.345 GHz) received outside the laboratory and rebroadcast onto the atoms.

articleTitle: Progress on the Optical Interferometer for the New Calculable Cross-Capacitor at NMIA
abstract: This paper details the recent progress made on the optical interferometer, developed to perform precision length measurements for the new calculable cross-capacitor at the National Measurement Institute, Australia (NMIA). We have confirmed both the alignment of the optical cavity to the capacitor’s axis using an external cavity set-up, and the proper functioning of the optical cavity after installation of the upper guard electrode. Development of the dual-frequency Pound-Drever-Hall locking system is ongoing, as is the iodine-locking for SI traceability. Current results are on track for achieving the targeted measurement uncertainty of 1 in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>.

articleTitle: Optimization of Wye-Delta-Type Quantum Hall Resistance Standard
abstract: Theoretically wye-delta transformation can be used to realize ultra-high resistances up to PΩ. For graphene-based quantum Hall array resistance standards fabricated to utilize the wye-delta transformation, a few challenges present themselves, including the unique quantized resistance in a graphene Hall bar and the limitation of the area of homogeneous high-quality graphene. In this paper, we discuss approaches to optimize the transformation for quantum Hall array resistance standard and propose a dual-output design for 1 MΩ and 100 MΩ as an alternative to other build-up techniques, shortening the path from quantum resistance standards.

articleTitle: The project ‘Metrology for Static and Dynamic Characterization of Supercapacitors’ – MetSuperCap
abstract: Supercapacitors (SCs) represent an environmentally friendly technology, that can replace batteries or work with them in high power density applications. To support the increasing use of SCs, accurate characterization is required under operating conditions. In addition, validated circuital and software models are needed to identify the SCs behavior in dynamic applications. Along with slower but highly accurate methods, novel quick, traceable, and effective measurement techniques are required to evaluate SCs State of Charge (SoC) and State of Health (SoH) and to promote the uptake of SCs in consumer electronics, energy, transport, aerospace and in many other applications. The MetSuperCap project aims to improve the characterization of SCs by providing an accurate identification of their parameters in the laboratory and under operational conditions.

articleTitle: High-Voltage Metrology for Electric Energy and Supply Reliability
abstract: The lower power quality and shrinking inertia of renewable generation puts new demands on monitoring, controlling and balancing energy flows in the electricity grid. This calls for new high-voltage (HV) metrology solutions to support the HV manufacturing industry. The recently started EU project ‘ENSURE’ is addressing this need by developing new HV measurement technology in four areas: wideband live connectable current or voltage sensors to monitor and calibrate substation instrumentation; new capability for determining the losses in power transformers caused by grid harmonics; new methods for loss determination in HVAC cables; and new partial discharge monitoring techniques for fault detection and localization in HVDC cables.

articleTitle: Improvement of the WR-5 Calorimeter at NMIJ Using a Novel Adiabatic Waveguide
abstract: In recent years, waveguide-type calorimeters have been developed for higher frequency ranges. The National Metrology Institute of Japan (NMIJ) has also developed a waveguide calorimeter capable of operating up to 330 GHz. As stated in previous work [1], it is crucial to take into account the effect of heat generation caused by transmission losses in adiabatic waveguides (AW) on measurement precision. Moreover, it should be noted that the isothermal control method at room temperature has certain limitations that have resulted in a worst-case relative expanded uncertainty of 12.7 % (k = 2). The purpose of this paper is to enhance the measurement performance of calorimeters by improving AW transmission loss. To achieve this goal, the newly designed AW structure, transmission characteristics, and adiabatic performance analysis will be evaluated. The low frequency region demonstrates improvements in the uncertainty of the WR-5 (from 140 GHz to 220 GHz) band calorimeter.

articleTitle: Octagonal Double Transformer SQUID sensors with Large Input Inductance for Cryogenic Current Comparator
abstract: Superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs) with large input inductance and octagonal double transformer were designed and fabricated using Nb/Al-AlO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>/Nb Josephson junctions for cryogenic current comparator (CCC). A 30-turn input coil of 1.5 µH is coupled to a large octagonal transformer of 3.6 nH. The counterpart of transformer is a 1.5turn coil of 3.0 nH coupled to a second-order gradiometric SQUID of 64 pH. The octagonal double transformer makes lowinductance SQUID easily match to the large-inductance input coil. At 1 kHz, a current sensitivity of 1.1 µA/Φ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, a flux noise of 3.7 µΦ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>/√Hz and a current noise of 4.1 pA/√Hz were achieved at 4.2 K. Another SQUID sensor with 10-turn input coil of 0.5 µH coupled to a large octagonal transformer of 6.0 nH, which is coupled to a first-order gradiometric SQUID of 580 pH, achieves a lower current sensitivity of 0.5 µA/Φ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and a current noise of 5.9 pA/√Hz.

articleTitle: Differential Measurement System based on Programmable Josephson Voltage Standards for low frequency ac voltage measurement
abstract: The paper discusses the validation of ac voltage differential measurement system based on Programmable Josephson Voltage Standards and commercial ac sources. It focuses on calibrating the fundamental effective value of low-frequency (62.5 Hz and 100 Hz) ac sine waves (0.75 Vrms). Preliminary results show that the relative consistency and Type A uncertainty under these conditions are better than 1 part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>.

articleTitle: Characterizing Voltage Transformers up to 150 kHz: A New Approach to Generate MV Distorted Test Waveforms
abstract: The increase in disturbances at frequencies higher than 10 kHz in Medium Voltage (MV) grids has led to new needs related to the characterization of Instrument Transformers (ITs) involved in the monitoring of these disturbances. In this context, this paper presents a novel generation and measurement setup for the characterization of MV Voltage Transformers (VTs) up to 150 kHz. The proposed approach is based on the generation of test signals composed of a tone at MV and power frequency and one at reduced amplitude and higher frequency. By implementing a suitable compensation technique, the traceability of the two tones is ensured before their combination.

articleTitle: High-Accuracy Current Amplifier for Small Electric Currents
abstract: A new instrument for the measurement and generation of small direct currents, the Advanced Laboratory Current Amplifier (ALCA), is presented. It is based on the concepts of the Ultrastable Low-noise Current Amplifier (ULCA) and aims for improved user-friendliness and cost-efficient fabrication while still achieving very low measurement uncertainties. Different ALCA variants are designed to cover current ranges between microamperes and sub-femtoamperes. The predicted parameters of two basic ALCA variants are evaluated and discussed. In addition, we show an initial long-term study of the uninterruptible power supply used.

articleTitle: Linking thermal converter AC-DC transfer difference with the AC quantum voltmeter
abstract: This paper describes a general technique of directly linking thermal voltage converters to the revised SI by measuring their AC-DC transfer differences using an AC quantum voltmeter. Preliminary measurements at frequencies from 10 Hz to 3 kHz demonstrate agreement with conventional characterization of better than 1 µV/V.

articleTitle: S-Parameter Bilateral Comparison in 4.3-10 Coaxial Line
abstract: This paper describes a bilateral comparison that was conducted between LNE and PTB on the measurement of S-parameters using an industry-grade connector, the 4.3-10 coaxial connector, typically used for telecommunications installations such as 4G LTE and 5G base stations. Among other connectors, the 4.3-10 connector is designed to have separate electrical and mechanical planes, leading to a low coupling torque. It provides a very stable passive intermodulation performance, independent from torque.Both laboratories used the same root of traceability using their own traceable Type N calibration standards and a traceable Type N to 4.3-10 adapter, but different procedures to transfer traceability to the traveling standards. Comparison results including uncertainties are presented.

articleTitle: Thermal hysteresis of travelling inductance standards
abstract: The international comparison CCEM-K3.2018 "Inductance at 10 mH and 1 kHz" is under preparation. To verify the uncertainty claims of the participant institutes, travelling standards of unprecedented level of stability are required. INRIM and PTB characterised several General Radio 1482 inductance standards versus large temperature steps that may occur during air carrier transportation. This work reports on the unexpected thermal hysteresis manifested by these standards which may impact on the uncertainty of the reference value of the K3 comparison.

articleTitle: Honey I Shrank the Kibble Balance: A Second Generation NIST Table Top Balance
abstract: Following the 2019 redefinition of the International System of Units (SI), the kilogram, as the unit of mass, transitioned from being tied to a physical artifact to a fixed value based on the Planck constant [1]. The adoption of simplified and compact metrology instruments has streamlined the traditional mass dissemination chain, making primary mass realization capabilities particularly valuable for calibration laboratories. For the past two years, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has been developing a second generation tabletop Kibble balance (KIBB-g2) aimed at realizing gram-level masses to ASTM E617 Class 3 uncertainties [2]. This paper provides an overview of the design and advancements of KIBB-g2, presents performance results, and outlines planned design changes for a third generation tabletop Kibble Balance (KIBB-g3).

articleTitle: Calibration of Wideband Current Transformers using a Precision Power Analyzer as Comparator
abstract: A measurement system is proposed for characterizing wideband current transformers (CTs) using a precision power analyzer as a sampling current ratio bridge. This approach simplifies the setup significantly with respect to conventional, primary measurement systems, with only a limited reduction in measurement uncertainty. Initial characterisation of the measurement system shows that it is able to achieve uncertainties of less than 50 ppm and 30 μrad for CT ratio error and phase, displacement, respectively over the frequency range from 50 Hz to 5 kHz, provided a calibrated wideband reference CT is available with suitably low uncertainties. This makes the system ideal for use by NMIs and in industrial applications that do not need the ultimate accuracies achieved by primary CT calibration setups.

articleTitle: Development of a 10 kV IVD and its Self-calibration Setup at Power Frequency
abstract: The present paper introduces the research of a 10 kV power frequency inductive voltage divider (IVD) and its self-calibration device. The two-stage 10 kV IVD used laminated silicon steel cores. The isolation reference IVD and the differential calibrator adopted double-layer shielding. The inner layer works as the equipotential guard to reduce the fluctuation of the reference potential caused by the floating potentials and improved the stability of the reference potentials. The repeatability of the self-calibration results was better than 0.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>, and the deviation of 10 kV : 100 V was better than 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> in ratio error and 1 μrad in phase displacement.

articleTitle: Internal validation of the whole resistance scale at CMI
abstract: The measurement range of resistance values in the primary laboratory of electrical resistance in the Czech Metrology Institute (CMI) covers 18 decades, from 0.1 mΩ up to 100 TΩ and is internally traced from the Quantum Hall resistor. Besides successful CIPM and RMO key comparisons, several measurement methods in the whole range internally approved the quality of the scale realization. Here, we discuss the realization and results of several internal comparisons. Some of them validated the CMCs, especially at low and high resistance ranges, where interlaboratory comparisons are not easily realizable due to the limitations of travelling standards.

articleTitle: One-Dimensional Median Filter for Frequency Transfer Applications
abstract: We present a study of a digital one-dimensional median filter for the removal of noise and prediction of data loss in frequency transfer applications. The median filter was implemented in an optical frequency transmission system where a 10 MHz signal from an atomic clock was transmitted over a 15 km optical fiber cable. We studied the noise filtering, data prediction, and stabilities, of the filter for different filter window sizes.

articleTitle: Travelling Ammeter for Supplementary EURAMET.EM-S45 Comparison on Ultra-Low Direct Current Sources
abstract: The subject of the ongoing supplementary comparison EURAMET.EM-S45 with nine participating National Metrology Institutes are direct current sources covering the range from ±100 fA to ±1 nA. The role of the travelling standard is played by a compound ammeter based on a transresistance amplifier, the ultrastable low-noise current amplifier (ULCA), and an 8.5-digit voltmeter. This set of instruments is completed by a Zener voltage reference standard. Investigations prior to the start of the comparison suggest that under optimum conditions a combined expanded relative uncertainty of 1 part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> or better can be achieved for at least the highest of the afore-mentioned current ranges. These highest demands require the use of a transportable thermostat for transportation between the pilot’s and any of the participants’ laboratories.

articleTitle: QuAHMET: Quantum anomalous Hall effect materials and devices for metrology
abstract: QuAHMET — Quantum anomalous Hall effect materials and devices for metrology is a Joint Research Project of the European Metrology Partnership. The project focus is on the traceable measurement and characterisation of quantum anomalous Hall effect (QAHE) materials as devices and primary resistance standard candidates.

articleTitle: Compressive Sensing Empirical Wavelet Transform for Precision Power Measurement Considering Interharmonics
abstract: Algorithms in the Fourier transform class, designed for power measurement, are notably influenced by interharmonics. Conversely, wavelet transform class algorithms are particularly susceptible to even harmonics due to band decomposition. This summary introduces a precision power measurement approach utilizing Empirical Wavelet Transform (EWT). The proposed method demonstrates the capability to achieve accurate measurements of individual power components under both steady-state and frequency offset conditions.

articleTitle: Research on Self-calibration Method of Current Comparator based on Reference Winding
abstract: A current comparator [CC] self-calibration method is presented in this paper.. It can guarantee that the inaccuracy of every component of the winding stays constant even when the CC is adjusted to a different ratio by winding the secondary winding of CC using a structure known as shielding drainage. The error of the CC ratio from 1:1 to 20:1 can be calculated by combining a reference winding with an auxiliary current transformer and performing a number of measurements and computations.

articleTitle: Development of a Topological-Insulator-Based Quantum Resistance Standard
abstract: This paper describes the characterization of the quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect resistor with Chromium-doped Bismuth Antimony Telluride with the efforts in coupling directly to a programmable Josephson voltage standard (PJVS) at zero magnetic field. The precision measurement of the QAH resistance was performed under the presence of microwave signal biased to the PJVS. Understanding such effect will help to improve the experimental set-up for integrating multiple quantum electrical standards in a single system.

articleTitle: Calibration of digital energy meters with IEC 61850-9-2 inputs
abstract: A system is developed for the absolute calibration of digital energy meters with IEC 61850-9-2 Sampled Value inputs. The meter under test is subjected to a stream of synthetically generated voltage and current samples simulating a poly-phase grid. Reading the meter before and after the test gives the accumulated energy. Comparing this value with a calculated value gives the error of the meter. This paper describes the error sources of digital energy meters and the test setup used to determine these errors. Small but nonzero errors in energy reading were found for some meters during tests that followed the tests defined in the IEC 62053-22.

articleTitle: Next generation Programmable Quantum Current Generator
abstract: This paper describes the latest improvements of the programmable quantum current generator (PQCG), which allow to get rid of the former 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−7</sup> relative corrections due to the resistance of the cable and extend the realization of the ampere over a wider current range, down to the µA range. Here we report on the first results of accuracy tests at 46 µA with a measurement uncertainty of one part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of the KRISS Kibble balance II : Focus on the moving mode
abstract: This paper delves into the research on the design and validation of a Kibble balance, with a focus on the moving mode. The Kibble balance is a technique precision measuring the kilogram using the Planck constant, and this study specifically concentrates on the effective implementation of this method. The Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science (KRISS) has been developing and researching Kibble balance technology, aiming to achieve a high level of accuracy through the development of a new Kibble balance. In this paper, we present the detailed processes and results of the design and validation of the Kibble balance, centered around its moving mode.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave Characterization for Dielectric Substrates and Conductors in 110-220 GHz
abstract: This paper presents the millimeter-wave characterization techniques for dielectric substrates and conductors by using a quasi-optical Fabry-Perot open resonator (FPOR). Compared with the conventional waveguide-coupled FPORs, the proposed resonator can simultaneously operates in the D-band and G-band. The position and the size of the feeding apertures on the spherical mirrors are carefully considered and a fairly high Q-factor of the resonator is achieved. The complex permittivity of polymer and the reflection loss of metal samples are accurately measured non-destructively in the range of 110-220 GHz.

articleTitle: Josephson-based calibration method for small-current calibration
abstract: In this paper, we propose a simple approach to calibrate small-current instrumentation based on Josephson voltage standards. Here, we have calibrated the 2-nA range of a Keysight B2987B electrometer by activating 2-12 Josephson junctions in a programmable Josephson voltage standard, and setting the calibration current by running the realized dc voltage through a 1 MΩ resistance standard to generate highly stable dc current levels between 290 pA - 1.74 nA. The results show drift of less than ±3 pA over a 15-minute time span and repeatability within ±0.9 pA for the selected current levels.

articleTitle: Real-time Detection of Modulated Radiofrequency Signals in Rydberg Atoms enabled by Optical Frequency Comb Spectroscopy
abstract: We present a method for measuring radiofrequency (RF) fields using Rydberg atoms. Instead of using a locked probe laser, we use a carrier-locked optical frequency comb to detect the time-dependent RF field. Using high-speed digitizers, we capture interferograms as a modulated signal dynamically shifts the energy levels of the system. This method enables us to simultaneously calibrate the RF field strength and read out modulated signals encoded within multiple EIT features in real-time.

articleTitle: Progress on the Opto-Electronic Bias for Pulse-Driven Josephson Voltage Standards at PTB
abstract: After demonstrating bipolar waveforms in 2020, PTB’s optical pulse transmission drive has been expanded for two independent Josephson junction arrays. Passive optical power splitters divide the two independent optical channels at room temperature. Balanced photodiodes modules in liquid helium then generate ternary electrical pulses to drive the nearby Josephson junction arrays via coplanar waveguides less than 10 mm long. The outputs of the Josephson junction arrays are connected in series and we successfully synthesized bipolar sinewaves at 1 kHz and 35 mV rms amplitude with higher harmonics suppressed by more than 96 dBc.

articleTitle: Characterization of a wideband high voltage reference divider
abstract: This paper describes the performance of a 200-kV wideband reference voltage divider for calibration purposes. The divider is constructed to have a flat frequency response from DC up to c. 10 MHz. The main use of the divider is on-site calibration of AC, DC and impulse measuring systems. It can also be used for calibration of VLF, combined and composite voltage measuring systems.

articleTitle: Verification of Power System Inertia Measurements
abstract: As the share of converter-connected power generation increases, new frequency stability challenges have arisen due to declining inertia levels. Grid operators need more accurate visibility of inertia to maintain system reliability. Many researchers have developed new methods for inertia monitoring, however, there is currently no standard verification method. This paper presents a proposed verification approach for commercial inertia monitoring systems currently trialed in the British power system. The development of the approach based on grid operator requirements and the measurement challenges under noisy transient power system conditions are described.

articleTitle: Evaluation of an Arbitrary Waveform Generator for Calibrating the Impulse Digital Recorder
abstract: This paper describes the utilization of an 16-bit resolution arbitrary waveform generator for calibrating the impulse digitizer. The generator can be programmed flexibly to create the necessary impulse waveform, which can be loaded via TDG software or an analytical math expression. Test results were validated through the convolution of the step response of the impulse digitizer and a reference waveform of known parameters.

articleTitle: A 30 MHz Phase Shifting Circuit for Calibration of Dual Channel RF Attenuation and Phase Measurement Systems
abstract: A precision 30-MHz phase-shifting circuit has been experimentally constructed for accuracy testing and calibration of dual-channel RF attenuation and phase-shift measurement systems. The circuit is a re-routing circuit that can recombine RF input signals with the same amplitude but whose phase can be set arbitrarily, resulting in calculable RF attenuation and phase-shift values.

articleTitle: Metrological characterisation of a commercial source-measure unit for small DC currents
abstract: We have performed a detailed characterisation of a commercial small current source-measure unit (SMU), the Keithley 6430, by calibrating it against an accurate reference current source on current ranges from 1 nA to 1 mA. The instrument shows a marked non-linearity at small fractions of full-scale, but over a period of four years its gain factor is stable to better than 50 μA/A on all ranges. This is sufficient for practical applications in metrology fields such as ionising radiation or photometry.

articleTitle: The grating interferometer with separated beams in joule balance
abstract: The multi-axis grating interferometry for multi-axial displacement measurement is investigated. Two spatially separated laser beams are used to ensure that the two frequencies of light do not share a common optical path before interference, which eliminates optical mixing and thus eliminates periodic nonlinearity error. Besides, decoupling of displacement along different axis is analyzed. The experimental setups are built for the test of the periodic nonlinearity. Periodic nonlinear error is smaller than 0.05 nm.

articleTitle: Dual-Frequency-Bias Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard Circuit Design
abstract: This paper presents a new 2 V programmable Josephson voltage standard circuit with dual microwave frequency input. This design provides three main features: (1) output voltages with nanovolt resolution, (2) the ability to perform a microwave frequency self-check based on a null voltage measurement, and (3) additional voltage output taps providing simultaneous 10:1 (or 5:1) divided voltage reference for resistive divider calibration.

articleTitle: An FPGA-Based Time-to-Digital Converter with Online Calibration Methodology
abstract: This paper introduces an effective online compensation mechanism for time-to-digital converters (TDCs) implemented on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), which are highly sensitive to process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variations. The online compensation strategy exploits the synergy between an external high-precision clock signal and the internal chip clock for real-time correction of TDC outputs. Our TDC architecture incorporates a coarse-fine counting scheme, complemented by a start-stop calibration module and a ring oscillator for precise time compensation. The proposed TDC system has been successfully implemented and tested on a Xilinx Artix-7 35T FPGA board. Measurement results demonstrate that our system achieves a minimum time resolution of 18.9 picoseconds (ps) and maintains a root mean square (RMS) resolution within 20 ps, even under temperature variations.

articleTitle: Measuring VHF Detector Linearity using a Quantum-Based Source
abstract: We demonstrate the use of a Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer (JAWS) for linearity measurements of two instruments: an RF power sensor and a fast ADC. The VHF-JAWS source consists of a chip with 12,810 Josephson junctions located in a cryocooler and driven to produce quantum-based ac waveforms at frequencies up to 50.05 MHz and power up to -19 dBm. We first confirm that the device is operating correctly by measuring the dc bias current quantum-locking range and then measure the system output power with an RF power sensor and a high-speed digitizer. After removing an overall scale factor, the ten-nanowatt scale differences between the programmed JAWS values and the measured values indicate better than ±0.5 % DUT linearity for frequencies in the VHF band.

articleTitle: Tabletop Electrostatic Force Balance for Liquid Mass Measurement
abstract: The design and operation of a tabletop electrostatic force balance suitable for measurement of milligram masses of fluid samples is described. The design incorporates a 4-bar linkage mechanism and provides a reference force based on electrical metrology of an integrated sphere-flat capacitor. The measurement is preliminarily validated using a test mass.

articleTitle: The integrated structure of force-measurement and guidance in joule balance
abstract: The joule balance method is a kilogram realization method based on the Planck constant. To further enhance its measurement capability, this paper proposes an integrated design method of force measurement and guidance based on the reciprocity principle. By studying the reciprocity measurement mechanism of the joule balance in dual modes, the reciprocity model is established. Based on this, an integrated design mebthod of force measurement and guidance is proposed. This method features high force measurement sensitivity and low linearity, effectively reducing the uncertainties introduced by misalignment.

articleTitle: High Accuracy Calibration Methods for the Input Stage of an Ultrastable Low-noise Current Amplifier without a Cryogenic Current Comparator
abstract: This paper describes high accuracy methods to calibrate an Ultrastable Low-noise Current Amplifier (ULCA). These methods are based in the use of Hamon transfer standards, high accuracy voltmeters and do not rely on direct or indirect use of a Cryogenic Current Comparator.

articleTitle: Characterization of the New CERN Metrology-Grade Digitizer Using the 10 V Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard at PTB
abstract: We present the characterization of a new metrology-grade digitizer carried out using the 10 V programmable Josephson voltage standard at PTB-Braunschweig. The digitizer was developed to meet the higher performance requirements for superconducting magnet powering in the High Luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider at CERN. By providing a practically noiseless test voltage from the Josephson voltage standard, it is possible to determine accurately the capabilities of the digitizer, which were seen to exceed the target specifications.

articleTitle: Flip-chip encapsulation of Graphene-Based Quantum Resistors
abstract: Achieving sustained stability of graphene-based quantum resistance standards has been the focus of many works with some major improvements in recent years. A novel approach combines existing solutions with flip-chip technology, offering compactness and electrical contacts without bond wires and integrating electrical shielding and encapsulation. Expected benefits include enhanced stability, maintaining quantum resistor properties over years, improved contact accuracy, and possibly better AC shielding. Though in development, initial outcomes suggest this technique could enable the development of more robust and versatile graphene-based AC and DC quantum resistors.

articleTitle: Vectorial Operation of a Bell-Bloom Atomic Magnetometer Assisted by Artificial Neural Network
abstract: This paper reports an all-optical vectorial operation method of a Bell-Bloom magnetometer. The spin projections in x and y axes are detected simultaneously by the dual probing beams configuration. And the vector information can be extracted from the phases of spin projection signals. By introducing an artificial neural network (ANN) to establish the relationship between signals and field direction, the phase errors are corrected automatically. With the assistance of ANN, the accuracy of the system has been greatly improved and dead zones have been eliminated basically.

articleTitle: Unperturbed Electric Field and Operator Current Towards Ground in HV Substations: a linear relationship between two measurements
abstract: As a part of the monitoring of the electric field (E-field) generated in HV substations, a proportionality was observed between the unperturbed E-field and the electric current flowing towards ground from the body of an operator equipped with insulating footwear, measured by an ammeter, in different substation locations. This proportionality cannot be assumed a priori, as the human body capacitive coupling with the HV and surround conductors in the complex substation layout can strongly vary, depending on the measurement point. In the paper, the validity of the proposed indirect approach is validated and quantified, considering an operator moving inside an HV substation. The rationale is discussed by a specific FEM analysis including an anthropomorphic body and confirmed through experimental validation measurement. The linear dependence between the unperturbed E-field and the current flowing from the operator to ground can help speed up and simplify the human exposure assessment to the E-field through indirect, but still sufficiently accurate measurements.

articleTitle: Specular gloss measurements from luminous reflectance by an absolute technique
abstract: Specular gloss is the perception by an observer of the mirror-like appearance of a surface.
