The specular gloss value is determined from the ratio of the measured luminous reflectance of a specimen to the theoretical Fresnel reflectance of the standard. Luminous reflectance has been measured by an absolute technique using the SIMT primary glossmeter, and resulting gloss values have been calculated. The measurement results agree well with theoretical gloss values, which validates the method and accuracy of our instrument.

articleTitle: A Criterion for Robust and Automatic Discrimination of the Stationary Region for PJVS Voltage Steps
abstract: Due to the presence of transitions in PJVS quantum voltage steps, the data at the edges of these steps exhibits low accuracy. In this summary, we introduce a criterion for robust and automatic discernment between stationary and transition regions within PJVS voltage steps. This criterion is established by bi-directionally searching for the minimum type-A uncertainty from the center to two ends of each quantum voltage step. We conduct experiments to validate the accuracy of this criterion within a 2.5 kHz frequency range. The outcomes of this research help to enhance the measurement accuracy of stepped quantum voltage waves and hence the AC voltage signal to be calibrated.

articleTitle: A New High-Frequency Inductive Voltage Divider for QHR Measurements at Frequencies up to 2 MHz
abstract: We report on the development of a new single-stage high-frequency inductive voltage divider (HF-IVD) for Quantum Hall Resistance measurements at frequencies up to 2 MHz. The design, construction and testing of the HF-IVD are detailed, including effects of switching on any spike voltages and settling times after switching are found to be only a few micro-seconds. Measurements over the 200 kHz to 2 MHz range show that both the in-phase and quadrature relative voltage deviations are less than 2% at 2 MHz. These measurements will also be compared to an electrical HF equivalent circuit model of the HF-IVD and presented at the CPEM 2024.

articleTitle: Research on Response of Vector SERF Magnetometer: Towards Unshielded Operation
abstract: For the purpose that release the high sensitivity capability of the spin-exchange relaxation-free (SERF) magnetometer to an unshielded environment by active magnetic field compensation, we investigate the response of a vector SERF magnetometer. A response model is built which provides a basis for the feedback controller optimization. A preliminary compensation experiment shows the potential of our SERF sensor to operate in unshielded environments.

articleTitle: Calibration of Autler-Townes based electrometry in Rydberg states of alkali atoms
abstract: Highly excited states of alkali atoms are a powerful tool for making SI-traceable electric field measurements without the need for an external reference. However, the calibration of these measurements suffers from ambiguity in which transition dipole moment to use. In this paper, we address this point, taking into account contributions from individual magnetic hyperfine m<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf> states and comparing theoretical lineshapes to previously published data. We also discuss measurement schemes that simplify this calibration by isolating angular momentum pathways.

articleTitle: Novel Impedance Standards based on Series-Connected Metal-Foil Resistors with Voltage-Supplied Encapsulations
abstract: We have developed 12.906 kΩ impedance standards based on a series-connection of four commercial encapsulated metal-foil resistors. The series-connection allows selecting single resistors whose deviation from nominal resistance value and temperature dependence have opposite sign and partially cancel each other. To avoid limitation due to the capacitances between the metal foils and their encapsulations, voltage is supplied to the encapsulations in such a way that this contribution is not only greatly reduced but that their residual cancels the residual parallel capacitance (at least partially). In this way, the total capacitance and the corresponding frequency dependence are strongly reduced, constituting excellent standards of impedance and time constant.

articleTitle: Measurement and Detection of Sub-synchronous Oscillations in Power Electronics Dominated Power Systems
abstract: As power converters gain a pivotal role in driving the energy transition of power networks, new electrical phenomena are emerging in the grid. Amongst them, a new type of sub-synchronous oscillation has been identified as originating from the interaction of power converters connected to the grid. This paper discusses the detection and measurement of sub-synchronous oscillations along with the instrumentation requirements.

articleTitle: Balanced-type Circular Disk Resonator for Permittivity Measurements in the J-band
abstract: A J-band balanced-type circular disk resonator (BCDR) excited by 0.26 mm coaxial lines is developed to realize material characterizations over the entire J-band. The developed BCDR has WR3.4 waveguide interfaces with coaxial-to-waveguide converters, which allows for the selective excitation of the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0m0</inf> modes in the resonator over a wideband. Owing to the mode selective behavior, the BCDR provides broadband material measurements of low-loss substrate materials. To demonstrate the developed resonator, the relative permittivities of cyclo-olefin polymer (COP) and perfluoroalkoxy alkanes (PFA) are measured in the J-band from 220 GHz to 330 GHz.

articleTitle: S-Parameters on Printed Circuit Boards for Cryogenic Environment
abstract: This paper describes how to calculate S-parameters in a reference plane on a PCB with unknown access lines. The technique is based on two taps on a section of the transmission line on a PCB. The application of this technique is cost-effective on-wafer measurements and cryogenic on-wafer measurements. In this proof of concept, a coaxial to coplanar waveguide transition is measured and compared to calculated results. This yielded differences of less than 0.09 dB up to 20 GHz in transmission.

articleTitle: In-situ electro-optic sampling of microwave signals applied to superconducting circuits
abstract: We report on electro-optic sampling (EOS) of microwave signals under cryogenic conditions employing a fully fiber-coupled measurement scheme. We use this setup to characterize the time response of ultrafast photodiodes at a temperature of 4 K. We additionally integrate a Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer (JAWS) to the EOS platform, which allows us to calibrate the EOS response, yielding traceability of the microwave measurements to a quantum standard. Finally, we determine the electrical reflection coefficient, i.e., the S11 scattering parameter, in a Niobium transmission line using EOS at different positions. Our work denotes an important step for traceable in-situ microwave measurements in superconducting circuits.

articleTitle: Automated coaxial IVD impedance bridge for the low value capacitance measurements at audio frequencies
abstract: This paper outlines the design and operation of a fully automated coaxial IVD impedance bridge tailored specifically for measuring low-value capacitances, such as those found in the Thompson-Lampard calculable capacitor (TLCC). The bridge is characterized by comparing a 2 pF capacitor standard to the LNE TLCC standard at a ratio of 3:8. It demonstrates excellent long-term stability and repeatability of 3 parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>. Such a bridge represents an invaluable instrument for investigating the Type A uncertainty of the TLCC setup and its various components.

articleTitle: Automated Accuracy Testing of AC Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment
abstract: In order to ensure correct metering and billing at public AC electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE), they have to pass a conformity assessment process in Germany. This paper presents an automated test procedure for accuracy testing of AC EVSE as the main part of their conformity assessment. The test setup is based on an electric vehicle (EV) simulator with real power transfer using a bidirectional electronic load. The reference measurements are done by a power analyzer, which is traced back to the national standards. Besides the test setup, some measurement results and uncertainties are shown.

articleTitle: Simulation and Compensation for the Amplitude Errors from Phase Random Jitter
abstract: This paper describes a simulation and compensation method for the amplitude measurement errors caused by the phase random jitter. For sinusoidal signal synchronous sampling, the phase jitter due to issues such as unstable phase lock of the commercial precision calibrator may lead into measurement errors when taking the average of multiple periods. The influence of phase random jitter on amplitude measurement was evaluated with Monte Carlo method, and the compensation method was deduced theoretically. The effectiveness of the proposed compensation method was verified through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: A New Type of Active Simulated Inductance Standard
abstract: A new type of active simulated inductance standard is proposed to achieve high-stability inductors that are endurable for transportation. The scheme is suitable for simulating inductors from the microhenry range up to the henry range with similar electrical characteristics. Two 10 mH simulated standards have been fabricated with a target long-term stability of 1 μH/H. These standards were initially investigated using NIM’s primary inductance standard.

articleTitle: AC Power Measurement Using the Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer
abstract: This paper develops a system using the zero-compensation (ZC) Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizer (JAWS) to measure an ac power of 220 V, 5 A, 60 Hz and power factor of 1.0. In the structure, an inductive voltage divider (IVD) converts the voltage of 220 V to 0.44 V and a current transformer (CT) converts the current of 5 A to 20 mA. The current then flows through a shunt and produces a volage of 0.4 V. The two voltages within 0.5 V are compared with two voltages produced by the dual-channel JAWS using two voltage comparators (VCs), respectively. Preliminary experiments are conducted to validate the performance of the system.

articleTitle: Preliminary Measurements on AC Quantum Hall Resistance in Graphene at KRISS
abstract: The quantum Hall resistance (QHR) of a graphene device was measured at alternating current (AC) using a digital impedance bridge. Aiming to trace the capacitance unit Farad from the AC QHR, first, 1:1 comparison between the QHR and the 12.9 kΩ resistance was conducted near 1 kHz. Next, the 10 nF capacitance was measured directly against the QHR at 1.233 kHz using a fully digital quadrature bridge. The measured capacitance values agreed with the reference values on the level of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>.

articleTitle: Investigating the use of a Coaxial Air Line as an Impedance Standard at Low Frequencies
abstract: Developing reliable standards for coaxial line systems in the AC-RF gap region has long proven to be challenging. In this work, the use of an N-type coaxial air line as an impedance standard at low frequencies is investigated through a comparison of measurements taken on an LCR meter from 0.1 kHz to 1 MHz with calculated values based on transmission line theory. The results demonstrate the viability of using such an air line as an impedance standard at frequencies below 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Cross comparison of HP/Key sight 3458As in 100 kHz DCV sampling mode using a Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: In this work, we study the performance of the HP/Agilent/Keysight 3458A in the DCV mode. A Programmable Josephson Voltage standard (PJVS) system was used to generate step-wise approximated triangular waveforms which were sampled at 100 kHz with an aperture time of 1.4 μs. We present the static gain error and non-linearity results at the highest sampling rate (100 kHz) for five 3458As. We find a consistent difference in behaviour for new Keysight-branded units compared to older units.

articleTitle: Highly Accelerated Life Testing of Bi–Sb Thermocouples in Planar Multijunction Thermal Converters
abstract: This paper presents the lifetime evaluation of the bismuth (Bi) and antimony (Sb) thermocouples assisted by the copper heat shunt in a planar multijunction thermal converter (MJTC) via highly accelerated life testing (HALT). The temperature is selected as the accelerated stress variable. The electrical resistance increment of the thermopile is chosen as the primary signal of failure during HALT. The mean time to failure (MTTF) of the MJTC is calculated at several elevated temperatures using a two-parameter Weibull model. The accumulative failure rate fits well with the Weibull model. The MTTF at rated condition was predicted using the Arrhenius equation. The analysis shows that the MTTF of the modified thermocouple design has a considerably longer lifetime than that of the original one.

articleTitle: Impedance Measurements at NRC
abstract: Calibrations of electrical impedance in the range of 1 Ω to 20 MΩ in the whole complex plane is done by a digital impedance bridge at NRC. Carefully conducted investigations over past years corroborate its metrological quality. The paper shows that best measurement uncertainties of some parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+7</sup> can be achieved with the digital impedance bridge.

articleTitle: Measurement and Calibration Approaches for Two-Port Scattering Parameters at mK Temperatures
abstract: This paper describes the set-up and characterization approaches to realize cryogenic scattering parameters measurements. The system developed at the Istituto Nazionale di Ricerca Metrologica (INRiM, Italy), exploits the short-open-load-reciprocal technique, to realize error corrected measurements. The system has been developed in the framework of the EMPIR project 20FUN07 SuperQuant, and it operates at temperatures down to the mK range, in the band 4-12 GHz in coaxial line. Calibration standards are referred to room temperature standards and computer-aided simulations are used to extract their behavior at mK. The first measurements on an actual device (a 20 dB attenuator) are here shown.

articleTitle: Comparison of a 1 nF Capacitor with a 1 kΩ Resistor Using a Digital Impedance Bridge
abstract: This paper reports our effort to improve a digital impedance bridge. The limit of the bridge resolution and stability is less than 3 parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> for the nominal 1:1 impedance comparison of two 100 pF capacitors. The Type A uncertainty for comparison of a 1 nF capacitor with a 1 kΩ resistor is about 1 part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>, presently limited by the stability of the resistor.

articleTitle: Accurate Comparison of Calculable HF Resistance Standards
abstract: This paper presents a one-to-one comparison of calculable resistance standards designed for radio frequency (RF) by using a digital bridge relying on the accuracy of two Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizers (JAWS). In particular, the frequency dependence of these new resistors over a range between 1 kHz and 80 kHz is analyzed. Preliminary results show excellent consistency in the measurement of these artifacts. The corresponding measured impedance values deviate, relatively to the lowest frequency measurement, by a maximum of 0.1 μΩ/Ω over the whole frequency range considered.

articleTitle: A visualization of electromagnetic fields in a kHz-band by utilizing atomic fluorescence
abstract: We are proposing and developing a visualization method of electromagnetic field in low-frequency bands by utilizing atomic fluorescence. In the method, a relationship between the cesium vapor atoms, a laser (852 nm), a magnetic field (9.2 GHz), a DC magnetic field, and a magnetic field in a low-frequency band (under observation) are used. In this paper, we report to be succeeded in demonstrating this proposing visualization method for a magnetic field at 105 kHz.

articleTitle: Research Progress on the Cryocooled 10 V Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard at NIM
abstract: This paper presents a cryocooled 10 V programmable Josephson voltage standard (PJVS) system including some improvements on overcoming the significant concern of thermal management and electromagnetic noise. The measurement results of operating margin have shown the minimum quantum voltage step of all 23 subarrays is 1.2 mA.

articleTitle: Pulse Patterns for the Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer
abstract: Delta-sigma modulator algorithms determine the desired sequence of quantum-based voltage pulses used by the Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer (JAWS) to create calculable, quantum-based voltage waveforms. We describe typical settings used for synthesizing JAWS audio-frequency waveforms and important additions to the pattern generation algorithm that improve the spectral purity of the JAWS waveforms.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of On-Wafer Test Structures for Signal Integrity Assessment at Chip Level
abstract: This paper presents the characterization and analysis of thin film microstrip line coupled test structures designed for evaluating Signal Integrity (SI) and Power Integrity (PI) up to 50 GHz on chips such as Field Programmable Gate Arrays. Several test structures were designed and fabricated on SU-8 photoresist thin film. SI and PI related performance parameters such as mismatch, distortion, crosstalk, and power distribution network voltage drops are emphasized by varying the dimensional characteristics of the test structures, such as the line width, length, bending and presence of neighbor traces. Additionally, calibration standards utilizing the multimode TRL calibration technique were implemented on the same chip to allow the test structures to be characterized by measuring their mixed-mode S parameters.

articleTitle: Application of the Kibble Balance Principle for Precision Measurement of Dynamic Torque
abstract: We developed a new dynamic torque generation machine based on the Kibble balance principle to evaluate the responsiveness of torque transducers used for dynamic torque measurement. This machine utilizes electromagnetic force to generate dynamic torque that is traceable in the International System of Units (SI) from electrical quantities. Using this dynamic torque generation machine, by measuring torsion angles and evaluated amplitude ratios and phases, we aimed to establish a more precise evaluation method of dynamic torque.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of the ADR1000 low-noise zener IC
abstract: This paper describes the performance results of the new ADR1000 thermally stabilized zener voltage reference IC from Analog Devices. Evaluation includes low-frequency noise, temperature coefficient, short-term and long-term drift measurements over the initial 588 days of continuous operation. Analysis included verification of the experimental setup employing an opposition zener array to maintain low uncertainty. Test circuit design, methods of the measurements and the uncertainty contributors are detailed in the paper. A noise reduction method by passive multi-cells zener array combination has also been tested. This comprehensive dataset provides valuable information to aid the development of the next generation of digitizers, voltage and current sources for electrical metrology applications.

articleTitle: Design of High-sensitivity Micro-Capacitance Detection Circuit
abstract: This paper presents a high-sensitivity micro-capacitance detection circuit designed for capacitive micro-displacement sensing. The circuit exploits the virtual short characteristic of the operational amplifier (op-amp) to achieve equipotential driven guard in triaxial cable, thereby mitigating the impact of cable parasitic capacitance. Additionally, the op-amp’s reference ground potential is allowed to float with the potential of the target capacitor, effectively overcoming the influence of parasitic capacitance to ground. Based on a self-developed three-terminal capacitive displacement sensor, it has been confirmed that the circuit possesses the capability to detect micro-capacitance variations at the zeptofarad (zF) level, thereby meeting the detection requirement for nanometer-level displacement resolution within the millimeter range.

articleTitle: Recent Improvements in SUT and METAS 4TP Sampling-Based Digital Impedance Bridges
abstract: This paper describes hardware and software improvements of the SUT and METAS four-terminal-pair (4TP) sampling-based digital impedance bridges. These improvements are based on the use of a new dual output coaxial multiplexer and modified software controlling the bridge and procedure of complex voltage ratio measurement. The new setup provides an improved accuracy of impedance measurements due to good symmetry of the circuit and averaging results coming from two digitizers.

articleTitle: The Recent Research on the NIM-2 Joule Balance
abstract: The National Institute of Metrology (NIM) proposed the joule balance in 2006. With more than ten years efforts, NIM has built two generations’ joule balance apparatus. In 2019 and 2021, the NIM-2 joule balance participated in the key comparisons of kilogram realizations with a combined relative standard uncertainty of 4.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> and 4.0×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> separately. At present, the main uncertainty contributions are from the alignment, external field, statistical, etc. To improve the NIM-2 joule balance, approaches including the integrated mechanism of force-measurement and guidance, a high resolution programmable current source, the synchronous measurement of the flux linkage and the displacement and the vacuum mass transfer apparatus, etc. are in progress and presented here.

articleTitle: Development of 10 kΩ metal-foil stable standard resistors
abstract: We developed three 10 kΩ stable standard resistors and evaluated their characteristics. They showed stable behavior and low drift rates in resistance within ±5 nΩ/Ω per year just after the fabrication. The temperature coefficients of them were less than 15 (nΩ/Ω)/K at around 23 °C, and the humidity dependence was within ±0.2 (nΩ/Ω)/% at 23 °C.

articleTitle: Research on steering atomic time scale based on a remote rubidium fountain clock
abstract: In this work, a rubidium fountain clock through an 84km commercial optical fiber link was used to steer the atomic time scale generated by a clock ensemble with 2 hydrogen masers and 8 high performance cesium clocks. The frequency stability of the steered atomic time scale reaches about 1.2E15@1d.

articleTitle: Grating chip design for miniature optical dipole trap system
abstract: This paper describes a primary design of grating chip for optical dipole trapping rubidium atoms. The chip is expected to achieve both magneto-optical traps and optical dipole trap simultaneously. The focus properties and diffraction efficiency of chip is analyzed to effectively constrain neutral Rb atoms in a dipole trap forming by a far resonance Gaussian beam. This miniature optical trap design can be used for application of compact quantum precision measurement system.

articleTitle: Pulse shape Optimisation of a Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer
abstract: Nowadays, precision electrical measurements in AC voltage are mainly based on the use of Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizers. Optimising the performance of such a system requires careful adjustment of the pulse train shape sent through the array. In this paper, we present a new method for tuning the various parameters of the pulse pattern generator when the Josephson array is operated in the zero-compensation mode. This method is based on the use of a two-terminalpair impedance bridge and can be fully automated. Preliminary results of this ongoing project show that the plateau width of the quantum-accurate output voltage increases by more than 2.5 times after optimisation provided by the described method.

articleTitle: Further Development of a Magnet System for Planck Balance Applications
abstract: An important part of a Planck, or Kibble balance, is the magnet system. It serves as an actuator in force mode and as a sensor in velocity mode. The performance of the magnet system in Planck balances is essential for mass calibration according to the International System of Units of 2019 [1]. This paper describes the further development of a lightweight magnet system for use in the Planck extension for high-precision vacuum mass comparators [4]. Based on the experience gained from investigations with a prototype magnetic system of the Planck extension, a further development of the magnetic system using simulation methods is presented.

articleTitle: Sub-Hz Frequency Dependence of New 1 Ω Standard Resistors Based on Nickel-Chromium Alloy Metal Foil Technology
abstract: When considering the dc resistance of 1 Ω standard resistors, frequency-dependent phenomena below 1 Hz down to a few mHz can noticeably reduce the comparability of results. This issue has been identified in the context of international comparisons between National Metrology Institutes. Recently, a new type of metal-foil 1 Ω resistors became available. Collaborative low frequency measurements involving NMIJ, PTB and BIPM showed the excellence of these resistors and the influence of cabling on this measurement.

articleTitle: Progress of Optical Measurement System Design for KRISS Kibble Balance
abstract: We report the design concept of a new optical measurement system for KRISS Kibble balance II. In comparison with the first generation KRISS Kibble balance, 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> generation Kibble Balance of KRISS adopt optical heterodyne interferometer. For a light source of heterodyne interferometer, frequency-stabilized 532 nm laser is being developed and laser beam is delivered through optical fiber. We also use silicon-oil pool and CMOS camera to investigate the verticality of laser beam guided to retroreflector on the moving coil.

articleTitle: Development of a Digital Multimeter with Removable Voltage Reference
abstract: We are developing a digital multimeter (DMM) system with a new concept of a removable voltage reference. In this system, the voltage reference in a DMM can be detached from the DMM chassis, used as a portable Zener voltage standard, and calibrated by using other reference voltage standards. This concept enables easy and advanced traceability of DMMs with lower maintenance costs. This paper presents the DMM prototype and the preliminary result of an experiment related to the drift characteristics of the gain error.

articleTitle: Research on the Linearity Test for the AC High Voltage Divider up to 1000 kV using a Stray Capacitance Divider
abstract: This paper describes a linearity testing method by employing a reference voltage transformer (VT) to calibrate the AC high voltage capacitive divider up to 1000 kV. The test results are verified using the developed stray capacitance divider with its high voltage arm formed by the capacitance between the high voltage circuit and a donut electrode. Experiment results show that the two methods proposed in the paper for the measurement of linearity are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Metrology for electric vehicle charging stations
abstract: The viability of electric mobility requires an adequate infrastructure of charging stations for both urban and interurban mobility, being the latter more complex due to the limited autonomy of electric vehicles (maximum energy stored in the batteries) and the time needed to complete the charge. The correct measurement of the energy transferred between the charging station and the electric vehicle (EV) also requires legal control to ensure consumer confidence and protection. This article describes the new CEM laboratory for testing ac and dc charging stations and its measurement capability with charging power of 30 kW and 300 kW, respectively.

articleTitle: An improved calorimetric thermal voltage converter
abstract: The paper presents the design of a calorimetric thermal voltage converter (CTVC) with a significantly reduced DC reversal error. It also includes the results of an analysis of the frequency-dependent component of its AC-DC transfer difference. The analysis was conducted using a mathematical model of the CTVC waveguide and heater, which takes the form of a microwave rod resistor. The validity of the analysis results was confirmed through laboratory measurements. The CTVC is currently recognized as one of the most precise AC voltage standards within the frequency range of 1 to 100 MHz.

articleTitle: N-turn Input Device for Calibration of High Current DCCT
abstract: A DC high current standard is important for calibration of DC power and energy meters for high current to support of EV charger infrastructure. The KRISS calibration system has been built with a high current DCCT as a key DC current standard. An n-times step-up procedure using n-Turn input device can be used to evaluate the current ratio of the DCCT covering a range from 10 A to 1000 A. We developed 9-turn input device which enables 9-times current multiple per step-up. The verification of 9-times multiple was carried out with a step-up of 1.1 A and 10 A. The accuracy of the 9-times multiple was verified within a type A uncertainty less than 5 ppm (k=1).

articleTitle: Research progress of electromagnetic wave measurement using cesium atoms at NMIJ
abstract: In recent years, the measurement of electromagnetic waves using atoms has gained global attention. National Metrology Institute of Japan (NMIJ) began researching quantum measurement in 2008 and has since developed technologies for measuring microwave power, free-space antennas, and visualizing electromagnetic waves. This paper reviews the progress of research on quantum measurement of electromagnetic waves using cesium atoms at NMIJ.

articleTitle: Single-cryostat integration of the quantum anomalous Hall and Josephson effects
abstract: By directly integrating a quantum anomalous Hall resistor (QAHR) and a programmable Josephson voltage standard (PJVS) into a single cryostat, we have implemented a unified quantum electrical instrument that provides a realization of the volt, ohm, and ampere in accordance with the revised International System of Units (SI). The quantum voltage output from this prototype ranged from (0.24 to 6.5) mV with combined relative uncertainties (k = 1) down to 3 µV/V. The colocated QAHR provided a realization of the ohm at zero magnetic field with uncertainties near 1 µΩ/Ω at R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">yx</inf> ≈ 25.9 kΩ. For the ampere, a longitudinal current applied to the QAHR is converted to a quantized Hall voltage, which was directly compared to the Josephson voltage, providing measurements of the ampere that are directly traceable to the revised SI. We determined currents in the range (9.33 to 252) nA with uncertainties of (41 to 4.3) µA/A, respectively. Limitations and improvements are discussed to aid the reproduction of similar instruments at other national metrology institutes.

articleTitle: Precision UHVDC dividers for traceable calibration up to 1200 kV
abstract: High voltage testing and metering beyond voltage levels covered by presently available metrology infrastructures are needed to secure availability and quality of supply. Calibration has been available up 1000 kV and there is a need to extend the calibration capabilities for testing and with voltage instrument transformers for sub-station metering up to 1200 kV. This paper presents the results of calibration of two precision modular UHVDC dividers, providing traceability to 1200 kV with an unprecedented measurement uncertainty. The scale factors and measurements of the two dividers were calibrated with LV resistance measurement, using a HV step-up procedure, and in two comparisons. The agreement of LV scale factors traceable to RISE and PTB is within 2 µV/V, and the combined expanded uncertainty for a measurement system is better than 15 µV/V at 1200 kV giving new CMC claims of 20 µV/V at 1200 kV.

articleTitle: Excitation noise analysis and excitation voltage optimization scheme design for fluxgate current sensors
abstract: Fluxgate current sensors play an important role in many fields such as industrial automation and power system monitoring. However, the presence of noise can seriously affect their performance. This paper firstly introduces the working principle of fluxgate current sensors, then analyzes the noise sources from the excitation voltage in these sensors, and optimizes the influence of the noise sources through experimental tests and theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: A Temperature Drift Correction Method for Microcalorimeter
abstract: This paper describes a temperature drift correction method, named as "low-frequency reference method", used in 2.4mm coaxial microcalorimeter system developed by National Institute of Metrology, China(NIM). Proposed method is used to trace the temperature drift during the long-term calorimetry measurement of a 2.4mm coaxial thermoelectric power sensor, and compensate the drift in measurement results. Compensated results indicate that the proposed method greatly improves the stability and repeatability of the microcalorimeter measurement.

articleTitle: Application of Electrical Standards to Torque Realization: A Device to Measure up to 1Nm
abstract: This paper describes the next generation prototype of the Electronic NIST Torque Realizer (ENTR) project. The first prototype version (ENTR-v1) has been able to realize low-range torques (on the order of 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> Nm) to uncertainties of less than 1000 parts in 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>. The second generation prototype (ENTR-v2) has been designed and constructed specifically with the goal of realizing at least 1Nm of torque utilizing a direct current, direct-drive design and traceability to quantum standards without the need for physical mass and length standard artifacts. The paper will describe some of the design decisions of ENTR-v2 in order to reach this higher range of operation, and we aim to present results of torque realization verification with a full uncertainty budget within the coming months.

articleTitle: Development of a WR-3(220GHz ~ 330GHz) Waveguide Microcalorimeter
abstract: This paper reports a WR-3 rectangular waveguide microcalorimeter served as power primary standard of China for the terahertz band from 220 GHz to 330 GHz. The WR-3 microcalorimeter measurement system and the structure design of the microcalorimeter will be described and measurement results of effective efficiency of a WR-3 thermoelectric power sensor will be reported.

articleTitle: Digitizer Linearity Measurement with a Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer
abstract: This article examines the non-linearity and gain error of a commercial digitizer on the 100 mV range with a Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer (JAWS) as a reference. Different digitizer input filter settings were studied, and the shortest aperture of the digitization window was chosen to maximize the processing speed. The results revealed a maximum non-linearity of 0.3 μV on the 100 mV range with the digitizer filter frequency set to 100 kHz. A gain stability over 12 hours was determined to be 0.92 μV/V.

articleTitle: Digital Bridge Voltage Ratio Calibration using an Automated Permuting Capacitive Device
abstract: An automated permuting capacitive device (PCD) was developed for the AC voltage ratio calibration of coaxial bridges. For user convenience and measurement accuracy, the permutation of the PCD capacitors was automated using a coaxial multiplexer. Our digital impedance bridge works at frequencies up to 100 kHz, and its voltage ratio needs to be precisely calibrated for impedance ratio measurements. The PCD can calibrate the 10:1 voltage ratio of the bridge for either the inductive voltage divider or the sinewave generators. The voltage ratio calibration using the PCD was studied and verified using reference values.

articleTitle: Computer-Controlled operation of PTB’s 80 V Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: After the proof of principle presented at the last CPEM, PTB’s 80 V Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard (PJVS) has been extended with a computer controlled bias source. This paper presents the development of a computer-controlled bias source for this PJVS. The compact 80 V PJVS can then be integrated into experimental setups like Penning trap experiments at the Max-Planck-Institute for Nuclear Physics.

articleTitle: Characterization of Closed-Cycle Toploader for Quantum Resistance Standard in Graphene at KRISS
abstract: We report on the preliminary characterization of a toploading closed-cycle cryomagnet for the quantized Hall resistance (QHR) standard at KRISS. A toploading probe, built with coaxial cables, is designed to realize QHR in graphene at direct and alternating current by utilizing a pulse-tube cryomagnet with a base temperature of 3 K and a maximum magnetic field of 7 T. To reduce vibrations, a mass reservoir and an acoustic enclosure are introduced for a remote rotary valve and a connecting flexible hose. The vibration-induced current in the coaxial cable of the probe is investigated as a function of frequency. We also investigate the degree of equivalence between graphene-based QHR in the dry toploader and GaAs-based QHR in a conventional wet cryomagnet with a 1 kΩ resistance reference and a cryogenic current comparator.

articleTitle: VSL 1200 kV Reference Measuring System for Lightning Impulse Voltage Calibrations
abstract: VSL has developed a new reference measuring system with rated voltage of 1200 kV for on-site calibration of lightning impulse voltage up to 3000 kV. The new measurement standard was compared with reference measuring systems from other national metrology institutes in a special comparison campaign. Based on the results of the campaign, calibration and measurement capabilities were realized in testing voltage ( ), front time ( ) and time-to-half value ( ) with uncertainties of 0.7 %, 3.0 % and 1.5 % respectively up to 600 kV and 1.2 %, 5.0 % and 3.0 % respectively up to 1200 kV. Together with additional linearity experiments, VSL is now able to provide lightning impulse voltage calibrations up to 3000 kV on-site. This reference system has been used for the calibration and further tuning of a 4000 kV damped capacitive voltage divider from the Delft University of Technology to improve its voltage and time parameters measurement accuracy.

articleTitle: Self-Calibrating Meniscus-Removal Liquid Permittivity Measurements in Q-Band Semi-Open Waveguide Cell
abstract: We introduce a novel broadband calibration-independent meniscus-removal transmission/reflection method for liquid permittivity measurements in a semi-open rectangular waveguide using a vector network analyzer (VNA). We utilize scattering matrices measured for at least five different volumes of the liquid tested to eliminate the effects of the systematic error terms introduced by the VNA with a test fixture and a reproducible meniscus shaping the liquid sample surface. This approach provides precise both, the height, and the permittivity of the sample solely from electrical measurements. The method is validated with distilled water measurements done in Q-band (33-50 GHz).

articleTitle: Ultra Low-Distortion, Low-Noise Transimpedance Amplifier
abstract: A transimpedance amplifier for use with a proposed ultra-linear current-output DAC was designed, implemented, and experimentally verified. The target precision was a signal-to- noise-and-distortion ratio (SINAD) of 122 dBFS, or 20 effective number of bits (ENOB), over a bandwidth of 100 kHz. Experimental verification was limited by the available measurement instrumentation, but the target was met.

articleTitle: Demonstrating the Versatility of a Josephson Impedance Bridge
abstract: We use the pulse-driven Josephson impedance bridge to perform quadrature measurements of two 10 nF capacitance standards and a 12.906 kΩ resistance standard at different frequencies between 300 Hz and 5 kHz. This leads to impedance ratios between 4:1 and 1:4. From these results indirect capacitance ratios were derived and compared with ratios directly at the same frequencies. This comparison agrees within Type A uncertainties for frequencies below 2 kHz. The largest deviation of 53 nΩ/Ω was found at the maximum frequency around 5 kHz. All measurements were carried out fully automated without the need to change the measurement setup, demonstrating the versatility of the pulse-driven Josephson impedance bridge.

articleTitle: Quadrature Bridge for Capacitor Non-linearity Measurement
abstract: A bridge is described that can measure capacitor harmonic distortion down to –160 dB. The requirements for the input signal generator are greatly relaxed by the action of a servo loop that produces a quadrature drive signal, while simultaneously suppressing common-mode signals at the bridge output. Measurement results were compared with simulations, leading to an estimation of the capacitor non-linearity model.

articleTitle: A Measurement Error Algorithm for EVSE Based on Charging Order Data
abstract: This paper introduces a cost-effective and high-performance measurement error algorithm that utilizes charging order data for monitoring the performance of Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE). The algorithm has undergone validation through on-site calibration and blind testing, demonstrating its precision and reliability. Consequently, the algorithm is well-suited for practical implementation in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Diamond Quantum Magnetic Sensor toward a Precision Comparison of Currents with a Current Comparator
abstract: In this paper, a diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) magnetic sensor toward a precision comparison of currents with a current comparator is described. A diamond quantum sensor can sensitively detect magnetic fields based on the Zeeman effect of the electron spin state of NV centers, which may be used as a detector in a current comparator. The compact diamond quantum sensor head has been developed, being capable of positioning in an air gap formed in a ring-shaped magnetic core. The sensor exhibited the DC magnetic noise floor of less than $100\,{\text{pT}}/\sqrt {{\text{Hz}}} $. The obtained magnetic noise floor is less than equivalent current noise level required for a current comparator.

articleTitle: Updates on the Mechanism for the Kibble Balance of the QEMMS at NIST
abstract: This contribution aims to describe the state of work of the new Kibble balance mechanism in the Quantum Electro-Mechanical Metrology Suite (QEMMS) at NIST. After experimental evaluation of a prototype flexure-based mechanism, upgrades have been incorporated in the design of a second version of the mechanism. These upgrades are mainly geared towards adjusting the linearity and direction of the mechanism trajectory, establishing the autostatic state, adjusting the static equilibrium condition plus stiffness in-vacuum, and rejecting external vibrations as much as possible. We hope to present measurements with the new design and put them in context with our improvements at the conference.

articleTitle: Heat Transfer Analysis of a Diamond Chip Resistor in Planar Multijunction Thermal Converters
abstract: This paper presents the heat transfer analysis of a diamond chip resistor in a planar multijunction thermal converter (MJTC). Diamond, with the highest thermal conductivity among all the natural materials, is of much interest as a chip material to increase the thermal efficiency of the MJTC. The temperature distribution along the diamond chip resistor and thermal response time of the MJTC are calculated for three different chip materials: aluminum (Al2O3), aluminum nitride (AlN) and diamond. The thermal analysis shows that the temperature distribution along the chip is significantly reduced due to the high thermal conductivity of the diamond, suggesting increased input voltage range. The calculated output voltage of the MJTC with the diamond chip resistor increases by 2 times and 1.2 times, compared with those of conventional Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and AlN chips. The thermal response time are 3.0 s, 0.9 s, and 0.6 s for Al2O3, AlN, and diamond, respectively.

articleTitle: Calibration and Fine-Tuning of a 4000 kV Lightning Impulse Generator Circuit and Divider
abstract: A lightning impulse (LI) voltage measurement campaign was held at TU Delft in October 2022 for the comparison between measurement systems of different institutes and the research of linearity performance up to 3000 kV. To achieve good agreements during the campaign, VSL, TU Delft and VTT characterized and fine-tuned the 4000 kV generator and divider. The front oscillations on the LI waveforms were reduced significantly by adding load capacitor to the circuit. The front time error of TU Delft measurement system was calibrated and improved by tuning the damping resistor of the LI divider using VSL measuring system as the reference. Final comparison campaign results indicated that the calibration and tuning had significantly improved the testing voltage and time parameters measurement accuracy.

articleTitle: Progress toward the Kibble Dynamic Force Reference
abstract: We present progress in the development of a dynamic force reference instrument (KDFR) based on the Kibble principle. We describe the operating principle and design of the KDFR and discuss how the design for alternating current (AC) force measurements contrasts with Kibble balances for mass measurement and necessitates additional corrections to the force calculation. We further analyze the coil impedance, a critical factor for correcting the measured voltage in a single-mode AC Kibble measurement and illustrate a scheme for calibrating its temperature dependence.

articleTitle: Recursive Star-Mesh Transformations for Resistance Standards
abstract: A recent mathematical framework for optimizing resistor networks to achieve values in the MΩ through GΩ levels was employed for two specific cases. Objectives here include proof of concept and identification of possible apparatus limitations for future experiments involving graphene-based quantum Hall array resistance standards. Using fractal-like, or recursive, features of the framework allows one to calculate and implement network designs with substantially lower-valued resistors. The cases of 100 MΩ and 1 GΩ demonstrate that, theoretically, one would not need more than 100 quantum Hall elements to achieve these high resistances.

articleTitle: Initial Characterization on the Magnet System of MSL Kibble Balance
abstract: This paper describes some initial characterization on the magnet system of the MSL Kibble balance. The magnet system has been designed to create a radial magnetic field in the annular gap that is shielded from external fields. The magnet system that consists of a ring-shaped permanent magnet housed in a yoke has been assembled. We report on some initial measurements of the magnetic flux density and its dependence on the air temperature. We have also evaluated the induced voltage to coil velocity (U/v) ratio of the magnet-coil arrangement using oscillatory moving coil.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Analysis of Vector Network Analyzer Measurements of four terminal-pair air capacitors
abstract: Traditionally, vector network analyzer (VNA) measurements have been used to determine the frequency dependence of four-terminal pair air capacitors. Recently, researchers at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) have used a four-channel VNA to determine the frequency dependence of air capacitors using the locations of poles and zeros of the capacitance as a function of frequency. This contribution describes the uncertainty analysis for the measurements of the 100 pF and 1 nF. capacitors.

articleTitle: Progress on the NPL, NMISA, RISE Kibble Balance Collaboration
abstract: This paper describes progress made by the NPL, NMISA and RISE collaboration on developing the "Next Generation" Kibble balance. Delays to the availability of the full size balances have concentrated work on the smaller Demonstration balances, which were developed by NPL to provide publicity for the redefinition of the kilogram. The Demonstration balances now work in an almost identical way to the planned, full size "Next Generation" Kibble balance, using the same software and much of the same electronics. This has allowed all three groups to solve problems and make advances that will speed up the work on the "Next Generation" Kibble balance. It will also allow the investigation of wider applications of Kibble balance technology using the software and compact electronics which has been developed.

articleTitle: Long-term stability of GNSS receiver delays in time and frequency comparisons
abstract: This paper analyzes the long-term stability of the delay of the GNSS receiver, compares the long-term stability of the zero baseline of the same module of receiver, and the long-term stability of the receiver of different modules. By analyzing the stability of GNSS receiver delay in two cases, it is determined that the main factor affecting the long-term stability of GNSS receiver is the hardware circuit. The impact of the hardware circuit and the underlying software on long-term stability is 0.7 ns. The impact of the time difference calculation method on long-term stability is 0.06 ns.

articleTitle: Design of DC Power Standard Source Based on PJVS
abstract: To meet the growing demand for high-precision DC power measurement and calibration, a quantum-based DC power standard based on ‘standard source’ architecture is introduced in this paper. This system integrates a dual-channel PJVS, high-voltage amplifier, large-current transconductance amplifier, voltage/current ratio self-calibration device, and other essential components. The standard power signal output by the system is directly used as a calibration reference for DC power measurement devices, and the combined uncertainty is expected to reach 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup> (k=1) at an output level of 1000V/120A.

articleTitle: Quantum Locking Range Effects in Pulse-Driven Josephson Junction Arrays for DC Voltage Generation
abstract: Pulse-driven Josephson junction arrays (PD JJAs) are used for the generation of arbitrary waveforms with quantum accuracy. The main requirement for quantum operation is that all the Josephson junctions have quantum locking ranges (QLRs) with respect to the power and frequency of the radio frequency (RF) bias and constant voltage over a range of dc bias currents. In this paper we investigate the QLR of PD JJAs for the generation of dc voltage. Our results demonstrate that in proximity to the QLR for RF power, the dc current-voltage characteristics can show apparent quantization of the voltage with statistical properties almost indistinguishable from those in the QLR.

articleTitle: Superconducting qubit coherence metrics for device engineering
abstract: Superconducting qubit coherence has a precision problem. Relaxation time T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and decoherence time T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are by far the most common benchmarks of single qubit performance in superconducting quantum circuits, and are heavily relied upon for engineering next-generation devices. However, these metrics have strong environmental sensitivities and are temporally unstable, and thus alone are not robust metrics for describing individual qubits and comparing them against one another.In this tutorial, the measurement and interpretation of superconducting qubit coherence metrics is detailed, and useful qubit metrics are outlined that consider current knowledge of T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> variation sources.

articleTitle: Quantum Hall Resistance Standards Based on Epitaxial Graphene with Different Doping Layer Sequence
abstract: Epitaxial graphene-based quantum Hall resistance standards (QHRS) can be operated at relaxed working conditions compared to conventional GaAs heterostructure devices. To reach the desired magnetic field working point, exact and reliable control of the charge carrier density of graphene plays a crucial role. This can be achieved by post-growth deposition of F4-TCNQ molecular dopants embedded within a polymer host layer. Here, we investigate QHRS with different sequences of such doping and undoped spacer layers to find a structure that is as simple and optimal as possible. By high-accuracy resistance measurements we found excellent metrological quality for all types of devices in a broad magnetic field range starting at 5 T and at 4.2 K. The resistance quantization is maintained over two years, so far, which gives further confidence in the robustness and long-term stability of such molecular-doped graphene-based QHRS.

articleTitle: Improvements of the Vertical Laser Alignment in Joule Balance
abstract: In joule balance, a vacuum compatible, verticallaser alignment method based on an oil mirror and air-spaced lens was proposed to measure and compensate the vertical deviation angle of the laser beams. This paper reports the improvements of this vertical laser alignment method in the focal-plane positioning error, off-axis error of lens and balance of oil mirror parameters. The method of double spots coincidence is used to locate the focal plane of the lens, and the optimal collimation region in the Gaussian beam is collected as the parallel light source. An observation mechanism is designed to realize the "on-line detection" of off-axis distance and the optimal area to balance the influence of "angular error of corner cube" and "off-axis distance of lens" is preliminarily obtained. The balance of the performance parameters of silicone oil has been initially realized.

articleTitle: Improving Rabi Attenuation: Toward a Quantum-Based Microwave Attenuation Standard with Atomic Vapor
abstract: Quantum sensing of microwave power has attracted increasing attention due to its various potential advantages. Recently we have demonstrated a quantum-based microwave attenuation measurement based on Rabi frequency, i.e., Rabi attenuation, using a cesium atomic vapor cell inserted in a rectangular waveguide. This paper reports on the optimization of the Rabi frequency measurement to improve the accuracy and dynamic range of the Rabi attenuation. As the first step in the optimization process, we reduced microwave detuning by carefully determining the resonant frequency. We also improved the method to determine the Rabi frequency. Consequently, we found that the Rabi attenuation corresponding to the change in power of the microwave signal generator was two orders less uncertain and one order more linear than in the previous study. These results pave the way for realizing a next-generation quantum-based attenuation standard with greater accuracy and broader dynamic range by further improving the Rabi attenuation.

articleTitle: A 120 A Wide-band Transconductance Amplifier Based on DCCT
abstract: This paper describes a simple solution to realize a 120 A wide-band transconductance amplifier based on a DC current Transducer (DCCT). Highly accurate output current with high bandwidth (150 kHz) can be readily delivered due to the low Common Mode Rejection Ratio (CMRR) error and low time constant of the closed-loop circuit, which benefits from the adoption of a modified DCCT. The transconductance amplifier is capable of converting 1 V into 120 A current output, with a bandwidth from DC to 150kHz.

articleTitle: The Quantum Electro-Mechanical Metrology Suite
abstract: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is building a robust open-source hardware and software Quantum Electro-Mechanical Metrology Suite (QEMMS) that can provide quantum voltage, resistance, current, mass, and force dissemination directly traceable to the new SI. The goal is to develop a self-calibrating SI system that is turn-key and fit-for-purpose for primary standard laboratories and other national metrology institutes.

Author Keywords: Graphene quantum Hall array resistance standard (QHARS)

articleTitle: A Dual Source Bridge at NMIA
abstract: The National Measurement Institute Australia (NMIA) has developed a dual source bridge (DSB) for resistance calibration in the range 1 GΩ to 100 TΩ. The DSB preserves our capability of using test voltages up to 1000 V, while improving automation and reducing measurement uncertainty. Preliminary measurements up to 100 GΩ have been compared between the DSB and commercial calibration systems.

articleTitle: Error terms and uncertainty analysis for flow calorimeter in RF medium-power sensor calibration
abstract: Flow calorimeter is proved to be an ideal solution for RF high power calibration with explicit traceability chain and low uncertainty. Error terms in flow calorimeter lack detail analysis in past research. In this paper, error terms of flow calorimeter is analyzed in terms of substitution error, loss error and mismatch error. Substitution error is analyzed by simulation of heat distribution. Loss error is described by attenuation constant of RF adapter, and is further proved by the experiment of a shorted power sensor. Mismatch error is measured by the vector network analyzer (VNA). In flow calorimeter of 10 MHz-8 GHz established as radiofrequency (RF) medium-power standard, these error terms result in 0.14% standard uncertainty in calibration factor of flow calorimeter. This calibration factor is further included in calibration of RF medium-power sensor or transfer standard (TS) as device under test (DUT).

articleTitle: Characterization of MV Instrument Transformers for Power Quality Measurement: the contribution from the IT4PQ project
abstract: Power Quality (PQ) monitoring in electrical transmission and distribution grids relies on the accurate measurement of wideband high voltages and high currents. Ensuring traceability of the measurements carried out is generally only partially accomplished by calibration of the low voltage (LV) PQ measurement instrument, whereas the calibration of the instrument transformer (IT) is mostly limited to the power frequency or performed at LV. In the paper, objectives and main outputs of the research project “Measurement methods and test procedures for assessing accuracy of Instrument Transformers for Power Quality measurements” (IT4PQ), which is focused on medium voltage (MV) grids, are outlined. An overview of the metrological framework developed within IT4PQ is given, together with details of the characterization of different types of MV ITs, both under controlled laboratory conditions and in the presence of influence parameters. Laboratory calibration measurement uncertainty is within a few hundreds of ppm and microradian up to 9 kHz, for ratio and phase errors respectively.

articleTitle: A 120 A Wide-band Transconductance Amplifier Based on DCCT
abstract: This paper describes a simple solution to realize a 120 A wide-band transconductance amplifier based on a DC current Transducer (DCCT). Highly accurate output current with high bandwidth (150 kHz) can be readily delivered due to the low Common Mode Rejection Ratio (CMRR) error and low time constant of the closed-loop circuit, which benefits from the adoption of a modified DCCT. The transconductance amplifier is capable of converting 1 V into 120 A current output, with a bandwidth from DC to 150kHz.

articleTitle: On the development of the high-speed precise arbitrary waveform generator HSWG
abstract: We report on the development progress of the high-speed, precise arbitrary waveform generator (HSWG) with a frequency range of at least 10 MHz. The goal of the development is to realize a high-grade generator that covers a frequency range beyond the ultra-stable high-resolution generator SWG, which is dedicated mainly to the 0.01 Hz to 100 kHz range. In this proposal, we present a new design based on our long-term experience with the development of SWG, addressing the needs of voltage, impedance, and power labs.

articleTitle: Calibration of Oscilloscope Rise Time based on Pulse Synthesis Technique
abstract: This paper presents a pulse synthesis technique developed at the Standards and Calibration Laboratory (SCL) for the calibration of rise time of oscilloscope. The principle is based on the application of a traceable reference of continuous wave to characterize the amplitude response of the oscilloscope under test (UUT). The pulse synthesis technique is applied to the output amplitude response of the UUT to facilitate the characterization of the UUT’s rise time. Calibration result of an oscilloscope by using the proposed technique was compared with that using the reference pulse technique.

articleTitle: Validating Low Frequency Measurement Capability for Multiproduct Calibrators
abstract: Fluke has developed a new multiproduct calibrator that can accurately source signals with frequencies below 10 Hz. This new capability poses a significant challenge to traditional calibration and traceability methods for AC measurements. In this paper, Fluke presents the results of low uncertainty measurement method using digital multimeter and its validation against Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard (PJVS) and thermal transfer standard .

articleTitle: Analysis and modification for RF low frequency leakage of the type-N coaxial thermistor sensor
abstract: This paper analyzes previous measurements of the effective efficiency of type-N coaxial thermistor sensors from 10 MHz to 18 GHz in Radio frequency (RF) power standard of international comparison. A dramatical decrease of effective efficiency is found at lower frequencies, leading to high measurement uncertainty. RF leakage is observed during calibration of the type-N coaxial thermistor sensor. The working state of the power meter is affected by the leaked RF signal, yielding lower calibration factor in previous results. In this paper, a filter circuit is designed to block the leakage of RF signals. Results with filter applied are proved by the manual open-loop method and the transfer standard (TS) calibrations.

articleTitle: Metrology Framework for Electric Vehicle Charging Stations in Canada
abstract: As Canada seeks to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, the replacement of fossil fueled vehicles with electric vehicles requires further developments in the related metrology infrastructure. In particular, standardized methods do not presently exist for measuring the high DC power levels produced by DC fast charging stations. This paper discusses ongoing work to provide calibrations and traceability for these measurements.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Remote Error Estimation Algorithms for Electricity Meters
abstract: Remote error estimation electricity meters is a novel technique with wide application. For testing the accuracy of a remote error estimation algorithm, an evaluation method using standard datasets is proposed in the paper. The errors of the meters in a standard dataset are known. After it is input to an algorithm, evaluation can be achieved by comparing the algorithm’s output values of errors with the known values of errors. Some experimental results are given with several standard datasets as input to a remote error estimation algorithm.

articleTitle: High accuracy magnetic moment measurement system using compensated Helmholtz coils
abstract: The uncertainty of instruments currently available for measuring magnetic moment is about 0.5%. To further improve the measurement accuracy of the magnetic moment for permanent magnets, a measurement system using compensated Helmholtz coils and a phase-locked method is developed. The coil constant of the Helmholtz coils is calibrated using null detection method. The uncertainty of the magnetic moment for the new method is 0.09%. The principle and results are discussed.

articleTitle: Power and Energy Generation and Measurement System to Support DC Charging of Electric Vehicles
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of a system for the generation and measurement of DC power and energy for voltages with magnitudes up to 800 V DC and currents up to 400 A DC. Power generation is based on the "phantom" power approach, where the voltage and current of the applied power are generated by separate voltage and transconductance amplifiers. Power and energy measurements are performed using a portable, DC transfer reference meter (TRM), consisting of commercially available instrumentation and transducers. Details of the system design, measurement techniques, and significant sources of error are presented.

articleTitle: Operation of Josephson Voltage Standard with Superconducting Shield in Magnetic-Field Environment
abstract: We have successfully operated a Josephson voltage standard (JVS) with a superconducting shield in a magnetic-field environment. This study involves mounting a NbN-based JVS chip on a custom-made 12 K stage adjacent to the 4 K stage within a dilution refrigerator. A magnetic field, reaching up to 10 T and generated by a superconducting magnet positioned 73 cm below the JVS chip, is initially reduced by a cancellation coil and further minimized by a superconducting shield comprising Nb, Pb, and permalloy. Consequently, clear Shapiro steps were observed under a magnetic field of approximately 10 T. This achievement marks a significant milestone toward facilitating quantum metrology triangle experiments within a single dilution refrigerator and conducting precise voltage measurements under extreme conditions.

articleTitle: Research on fF Range on-chip Capacitance Standard
abstract: The femtofarad (fF) range on-chip capacitance standard has been designed and fabricated. Guided by the theoretical calculations and simulation analysis, capacitances in the range of 10 fF-100 fF with an accurate step of 10 fF have been achieved using an interdigital capacitance standard by means of incremental capacitance. The accuracies of these capacitors are better than 5%, and the typical measurement uncertainty is less than 0.5%×C+100 aF (k=2) where C is the nominal value of capacitor.
